Read this before any other protocol. It governs how the protocols themselves
change, and the telemetry duties that make the project usable as research data.

## Standing principles

1. **Protocols are normative until amended.** An agent that finds a protocol
   wrong, ambiguous, or costly does not silently deviate: it follows the
   protocol (or stops), records the friction in
   `results/telemetry/events.md`, and proposes an amendment — a dispatched
   worker proposes it to the operator; the operator amends directly under the
   procedure below, an `events.md` incident being a sufficient trigger.  Owner
   sign-off is needed only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.
2. **Amendments are evidence-driven.** Every change to a file under
   `local/protocols/` or to `AGENTS.md` must append an entry to
   `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` citing its trigger: an `events.md` incident,
   a telemetry observation (e.g. repeated duplicate builds in
   `builds.jsonl`), or an upstream policy decision by the user. No trigger,
   no amendment.
3. **The parent repo is precedent, not law.** The GitHub-era mechanism (frozen
   under `.github/`, mapped in `local/DESIGN.md`) is the default answer to
   "how should this work?"; deviations are fine when the local setting
   genuinely differs, and must be recorded in `EVOLUTION.md` with the reason.
4. **De-automation is a valid evolution step.** The parent workflow repeatedly
   demoted LLM agents to deterministic scripts once the mechanical half of a
   job was understood (issue-automation.yml:13-21), and demoted CI jobs to
   notices when resources were exhausted. Prefer the cheapest mechanism that
   holds the invariant.
5. **Two memory disciplines.** Reports and session records are append-only and
   never rewritten (supersede with dated status notes). Protocol documents
   and paper-gap notes are living documents that are rewritten in place
   (history lives in git and `EVOLUTION.md`). Do not mix the two.

## Amendment procedure

1. Write the incident/observation in `results/telemetry/events.md` (dated).
2. Draft the protocol edit.
3. Append to `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`:
   `## YYYY-MM-DD — <short title>` with fields **Trigger** (cite events.md
   entry or telemetry line), **Change** (files + gist), **Expected effect**,
   and, when known later, **Outcome**.
4. Commit protocol edit and ledger entry together, `docs(local)` scope.
5. If the change alters guard semantics (locks, caps, gates, kill switches),
   grep `local/` for every enforcement point and update all of them in the
   same commit — the parent repo maintained such consistency invariants
   through cross-referencing comments; we inherit the same drift risk.

## Telemetry duties

Schemas (all JSONL, one object per line; timestamps ISO-8601 with offset):

- `results/telemetry/stages.jsonl` —
  `{ts, stage, event: start|end|milestone, note?, tokens_note?}`
  Stages: `1-skeleton`, `2-references`, `3-blueprint`, `4.1-minimal`,
  `4.2-full-skeleton`, `4.3-proofs` (extend as needed).
- `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` —
  `{name, role, issue, pr?, thread_id, start, end, wall_s,
    usage: {input, cached_input, cache_write, output, reasoning},
    exit, dispatcher, worktree, status: active|done|failed|archived}`
  Written only by `local/bin/dispatch.sh` / `telemetry.py`.
- `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` —
  `{ts, kind: warm|rebuild|cache-get|ci-build, trigger, seconds, outcome,
    sha?, note?}`
- `results/telemetry/events.md` — dated bullets; free prose; one incident per
  bullet: symptom → diagnosis → fix → lesson.

Duties:

- **Every agent session goes through `dispatch.sh`** so token usage and wall
  time land in `sessions.jsonl`. A session started any other way is a
  telemetry hole; if one happens, backfill a line with `dispatcher: manual`.
- **Every full build** (warmer, CI, cold rebuild) lands in `builds.jsonl`.
- **Stage transitions** are logged by the orchestrator (main session) at the
  moment they happen, not reconstructed later.
- Claude-side (non-codex) subagent fleets are summarized into `stages.jsonl`
  as `milestone` entries with token totals, since they bypass `dispatch.sh`.

## Research-data invariants

The project doubles as a study of a self-evolving formalization workflow.
Three artifacts must therefore stay trustworthy:

- `EVOLUTION.md` — complete: every protocol change has an entry.
- `events.md` — honest: failures are recorded as failures, including agent
  mistakes, wasted builds, and reverted work.
- `sessions.jsonl` + `stages.jsonl` — quantitative: per-stage cost
  (time, tokens, session counts) reconstructible by a script, not by memory.

# Local Operations Layer — Architecture

This repository is a local-only continuation of the workflow that
[LionSR/MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE) evolved on GitHub while
formalizing the low individual degree test (LDT, arXiv:2009.12982). The active
track here is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from MIP\*=RE
(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and NEEXP in MIP\* (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).

Every GitHub-hosted operation of the parent workflow is replaced by a local
equivalent that *executes* here. Since 2026-09-01 the issue, PR, evidence and
merge **records** live on GitHub again (`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`,
`protocols/issues-prs.md`); what runs is still local. The `.github/` tree is
kept **frozen as reference** — it documents the mechanisms being localized and
is never executed here. The operative layer is this `local/` tree plus the
(already-local) `scripts/` audits and `.githooks/` gates, which port
unchanged.

## Layout

```
local/
├── DESIGN.md          # this file — architecture and invariants
├── README.md          # operator's entry point: commands, lifecycle walkthrough
├── protocols/         # normative protocol documents
│   ├── meta.md        # how protocols evolve; telemetry duties (read first)
│   ├── build-cache.md # hot main cache; no-duplicate-compilation rules
│   ├── ci.md          # local PR CI gate
│   ├── review.md      # reviewer dispatch and gating
│   ├── autofix.md     # auto-fix loop, iteration caps
│   ├── issues-prs.md  # GitHub-backed issue and PR lifecycle
│   ├── sessions.md    # agent session naming, dispatch, archiving
│   └── EVOLUTION.md   # dated protocol-amendment ledger (research data)
├── personas/          # system prompts for locally dispatched agents
└── bin/               # executables (the workflow engine)
local/briefs/          # per-issue design briefs (committed)
results/telemetry/     # sessions/stages/builds logs, GitHub snapshot (committed)
```

Runtime state that must never be committed lives in `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/`
(hot cache, snapshots, locks, served site) and `.worktrees/` (gitignored). An
absolute `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` may instead hold branch-private `.lake` products.

## GitHub → local mapping

| GitHub mechanism | Local replacement |
|---|---|
| PR CI (`pr-ci.yml`) on push/PR events | `local/bin/ci.sh <pr-id>` run by the PR lifecycle scripts |
| Main-build actions cache (main-only save, PR restore) | Hot main cache: single-writer warmer + read-only snapshots + APFS copy-on-write clones per worktree (`build-cache.md`) |
| `lake exe cache get` (Mathlib cloud cache) | Unchanged — already local |
| Model-backed PR review chained on CI success | `local/bin/review.sh <pr-number>`: codex CLI with the same `.github/prompts/` review personas, invoked only from green exact-head CI statuses; one COMMENT review plus `local-review/summary` |
| Auto-fix workflows (CI-fix, blueprint-fix, review-fix) | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode {ci,blueprint,review,auto}` with the same commit-prefix guards and a combined iteration cap |
| `@claude`/`@codex` mention responders | `local/bin/agent.sh <id> "instruction"` — human-invoked codex session on the branch worktree |
| GitHub issues + sub-issues + labels | unchanged — GitHub is the record again (`issues-prs.md`); `issue_new.py` / `issue_close.py` drive it through `gh_common.py` |
| GitHub PRs | GitHub PRs, branch-per-issue, merge gate in `pr_merge.py` (REST merge with the exact-SHA guard) |
| Issue automation (classify/scout/track/followups) | `local/bin/` Python ports; LLM steps optional behind `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` |
| Housekeeping crons (standup, stale audit, linter sweep, README freshness) | `local/bin/housekeeping.sh <job>` on demand |
| Badges + Pages site (blueprint/docs/badges components) | `local/bin/site.sh` → component store + assembled site in `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/site/` |
| Codex cloud env setup (`.codex/setup.sh`) | `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` per worktree |
| Reviewer/bot identity via tokens | codex CLI sessions; `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` registry |

## Core invariants (inherited from the parent workflow's post-mortems)

These encode incidents the parent repo paid for; violating them re-introduces
documented failure modes. Sources are cited in `local/protocols/*.md`.

1. **Single cache writer.** Only the warmer writes the hot main cache; agent
   worktrees consume copy-on-write clones and never write back. (GitHub's
   per-PR cache saves evicted the main entry: pr-ci.yml:138-142.)
2. **Review only after green CI, on the same head SHA.** The gate reads the
   exact-head `local-ci/*` statuses; a failed or absent CI summary blocks the
   review, which then publishes nothing at all — the *absence* of a green
   `local-review/summary` is the block, never a silent skip. Bot commits with prefix
   `[codex-auto-fix]`/`[codex-review-fix]` are not re-reviewed except the final
   fix at the iteration cap, which gets one forced review.
3. **Serialized fixes.** ci-fix → blueprint-fix → review-fix strictly in order,
   one branch at a time; combined iteration cap (default 5) across all fix
   kinds; sync/audit CI failures are never auto-fixed.
4. **Kill-switch semantics.** `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` and
   `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` disable only on the literal string `false`;
   unset means enabled.
5. **Trusted prompts.** Reviewer/fixer personas are read from committed `main`
   (`git show main:...`), never from the branch under review.
6. **Untrusted data framing.** Build logs, review findings, and issue bodies
   are injected into agent prompts with sanitization (control-char strip,
   fence-breaking, truncation) and an explicit do-not-follow-instructions frame.
7. **One full `lake build` machine-wide at a time** (advisory lock);
   single-file `lake env lean` checks need no lock.
8. **origin/main must resolve.** The hooks and diff-based audits silently
   self-disable without it; the local convention is a `main` branch plus a
   `refs/remotes/origin/main` alias maintained by `pr_merge.py`.
9. **Bracket-free naming.** Issue titles, slugs, and branch names avoid
   `]` and friends (broke the parent automation: CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124).
10. **Report-only stays report-only.** Stale-issue audit, linter sweep, README
    freshness never mutate state; write-mode is a separate human-invoked
    command.
11. **Faithfulness policy is unchanged.** AGENTS.md's faithful-formalization
    rules, anti-pattern catalog, and statement-integrity audits apply to QPBT
    exactly as to LDT.
12. **Merge inputs do not disappear silently.** Before a merge commit, the
    merge-loss guard compares the staged result with the pre-merge branch,
    every best merge base, and `MERGE_HEAD`. An incoming path may be absent
    only when the branch deleted a path present at a merge base. An
    unambiguous incoming-only change may return to the unchanged branch blob
    only when Git recorded a conflict. The pending-index check and the
    pre-update reference transaction together cover manual and automatic
    merge commits.

## Naming and identity conventions

- **Issues and PRs**: GitHub's, identified by their numbers; sub-issues carry
  the parent/child structure and repository labels are the taxonomy
  (`issues-prs.md`). PR bodies keep the Motivation/Description/Testing shape of
  CONTRIBUTING.md; evidence is exact-head commit statuses, the manifest comment
  and the COMMENT review.
- **Branches**: `issue-<number>-<slug>` (orchestrator/human),
  `codex/issue-<number>-<slug>` (agent-created); the number is the GitHub
  issue's.
- **Fix commits**: `autofix.sh`'s subjects are prefixed `[codex-auto-fix]` /
  `[codex-review-fix]` exactly (the review-gate skip regex depends on them);
  operator and worker repairs use plain `fix(...)` subjects and are reviewed.
- **Codex sessions**: `<role>-<issue|scope>-<yyyymmdd>-<seq>` with roles
  `orc, prover, reviewer, simplifier, blueprint, splitter, scout`, plus
  `mathfix` for astra after its availability is reported on #26.
  Dispatched only via `local/bin/dispatch.sh`, which records the codex `thread_id`,
  captures the `--json` event stream to
  `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl`, and appends a summary line to
  `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`. Archiving a session = final status line
  in the registry + worktree removal; the JSONL capture is the archive.

## Telemetry (research-paper data)

All appends are one-line JSON; schemas documented in `protocols/meta.md`.

- `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` — one line per agent session: name, role,
  issue/pr, thread_id, start/end, wall seconds, token usage (input, cached,
  output, reasoning), exit status, dispatcher.
- `results/telemetry/stages.jsonl` — one line per project stage/substage
  transition with timestamps and manual token/agent tallies.
- `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` — one line per full build / cache event:
  kind (warm, rebuild, cache-get), duration, outcome, trigger.
- `results/telemetry/events.md` — dated free-form incident log (what broke,
  diagnosis, fix); the raw feed for `protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.
- `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` — dated protocol amendments: cause (cite an
  `events.md` entry or telemetry), the change, expected effect. This file is
  the primary record of workflow self-evolution.

## Model policy

- codex CLI (`gpt-5.6-sol`, ultra effort) drives orchestrator/prover/reviewer/
  simplifier sessions (`codex exec`, `codex exec review`); `dispatch.sh` also
  admits the `mathfix` role for astra only after `owner-tools/astra-poll.sh`
  reports availability on #26.
- Claude-side subagents: easy/mechanical tasks run on Opus-tier. The current
  `mathfix` lane is Claude Fable 5.1, launched by the owner session through its
  Agent tool and recorded in `results/telemetry/owner-sessions.jsonl`; Fable
  otherwise remains reserved for hard reasoning (proof strategy, protocol
  synthesis, adversarial verification).
- Reviewer and prover roles must be **different sessions** — a session never
  reviews its own diff.

# Build cache protocol — the hot main cache

Normative. This document specifies the local replacement for the parent
workflow's GitHub Actions build cache, and the rules every worktree must obey to
avoid duplicate compilation. It is the protocol behind three executables:

| script | role |
|---|---|
| `local/bin/cache-warmer.sh` | the **single writer**: builds `main`, publishes read-only snapshots |
| `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh` | the **consumer**: keyhash-gated copy-on-write clone into a worktree |
| `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` | fresh-worktree bootstrap (replaces `.codex/setup.sh`) |

Governing invariants: `local/DESIGN.md` #1 (single cache writer) and #7 (one full
`lake build` machine-wide). Where this document and `DESIGN.md` disagree,
`DESIGN.md` wins.

---

## 1. What is being replaced, and why it was built that way

The parent repository's caching design is the residue of a specific, documented
failure. The load-bearing citations:

| parent mechanism | citation | what it encodes |
|---|---|---|
| Split restore/save, save only on `main` | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:137-167` | *"The cache is saved only from main and restored everywhere."* |
| `lean-action`'s own cache disabled | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:138-142` | The post-mortem: a ~2.6 GB entry saved **per PR run** cycled through the 10 GB repository cache budget and evicted the main-branch entry, *"so no run ever restored usable MIPStarRE oleans and every run rebuilt the whole library."* |
| Same policy restated in the weekly job | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:75-77` | *"See pr-ci.yml: per-run lake caches evict the main build cache from the repository cache budget."* |
| Main runs exempt from cancellation | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:50` | *"Do not cancel main-branch runs: they seed the build cache."* |
| Save runs `if: always()` on main | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:161-162` | *"Save even when the build failed: a partial cache still spares the next run the modules that did compile."* |
| ProofWidgets prune workaround | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:56-69` | A fresh-tree upstream bug that aborts the entire Mathlib cache fetch |
| `elan` install isolated from the cache lifecycle | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:44-54` | Avoids *"a partial cache save or restore-then-overwrite that could negate the ProofWidgets workaround"* |
| Independent cache for the doc subproject | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:135-140` | `docbuild/` is its own Lake project with its own key |
| Mathlib bumps are manual only | `.github/workflows/update.yml:3-5` | A bump *"triggers a full library rebuild and possibly an auto-fix cascade"* |
| Lean setup removed from a PR job | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:314` | A job was demoted to a notice *"after repeated runner disk exhaustion"* |

The single sentence to carry forward: **many writers destroyed the one valuable
cache entry.** Every rule below exists to make that impossible locally, where the
same failure mode reappears as parallel agent worktrees writing into a shared
build tree.

---

## 2. The two-tier split

`.lake/` holds two caches with different provenance, different lifetimes, and
different sharing rules. Conflating them is the primary way to reintroduce the
parent's failure.

An absolute `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` relocates `.lake` to `<root>/<branch>`. The
shared helper uses canonical paths to reject `/`, checkout or `hot-main` overlap,
escape, or ownership by another branch or detached worktree. Existing data is
not moved. Keep it exported for dispatch `--add-dir` and post-merge cleanup.

**Tier 1 — `.lake/build`** — this project's own compiled artifacts (`.olean`,
`.ilean`, `.c`, `.trace` for `MIPStarRE` modules). This is *exactly* what the
parent cached, and only from `main`. Locally it is produced by the warmer and
distributed as copy-on-write clones. Each worktree owns a **private, writable**
copy.

**Tier 2 — `.lake/packages`** — Mathlib and its transitive dependencies. The
parent never put these in the GitHub cache; they come from Mathlib's own cloud
cache via `lake exe cache get` inside `lean-action`. Locally they live **once
per manifest** in a shared, read-only store:
`$CACHE_ROOT/packages/<key>`, `key = sha256(lake-manifest.json ‖ lean-toolchain)[:16]`,
and every worktree's `.lake/packages` is a symlink to it.

> **Why a shared store is safe here (2026-09-03).** The old objection — a
> shared tree is read-only only by convention, so one `lake update` mutates it
> for everyone — is answered mechanically: the store is `chmod -R a-w`, so any
> write (an automated `lake update`, a dependency rebuild after a manifest
> drift) fails loudly in the one worktree that attempted it. Identity is by
> key, so a Mathlib bump simply creates a new store entry; worktrees on the old
> manifest keep linking the old one. The first worktree to need a key fetches
> with `lake exe cache get` into a real directory, then *publishes* it (move,
> `chmod a-w`, link); later worktrees only link. Cost: 7.3 GB once per key
> instead of per worktree (8 copies = 58 GB on 2026-09-03, on a 97 % full disk).
> `worktree-setup.sh` still refuses to run `lake update`.

Consequence for `lake update`: it is not part of any automated path here. It
rewrites `lake-manifest.json`, which moves the cache key (§3) out from under
every published snapshot, and it mutates vendored package checkouts. Mathlib
bumps stay human-invoked, exactly as `update.yml:3-5` argues.

## 3. The cache key

```
keyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )
```

concatenated in that fixed order, `‖` being byte concatenation. This is the local
analog of `hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json', 'lakefile.toml')` in
`pr-ci.yml:143-149`. The definition is duplicated verbatim in `cache-warmer.sh`
and `warm-worktree.sh` (function `compute_keyhash`); the two copies **must stay
byte-identical**, or every consumer silently and permanently takes the cold path.
A missing input file is a hard error, never a default.

Two properties matter, and they are not symmetric:

1. **A snapshot may be older than the consumer's base commit.** The parent's
   `restore-keys` deliberately drop the SHA suffix and prefix-match the newest
   entry under the same hash. This is safe because Lake's staleness test is
   trace-hash based, not mtime based: a cloned artifact whose inputs still hash
   equal is reused, and everything else is rebuilt. Cloned files therefore do not
   need their timestamps preserved.
2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,
   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.
   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`
   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls
   back to the cold path. It never partially reuses.

## 4. On-disk layout

Shared packages and `hot-main` use `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT`; branch products may
use `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` as in §2. Neither runtime tree is committed.

```
~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/
├── .full-build-lock/            # machine-wide: one full `lake build` at a time
│   └── info                     # pid, host, started, started_epoch, purpose
├── .telemetry-lock/             # short-lived; serializes JSONL appends
├── logs/                        # captured build logs (warm-*.log, worktree-build-*.log)
└── hot-main/
    ├── .writer-lease/           # only the warmer holds this
    │   └── info
    ├── repo/                    # the always-warm detached checkout of main
    ├── snapshots/
    │   ├── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/
    │   │   ├── STAMP
    │   │   └── build/           # a byte copy of repo/.lake/build
    │   └── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/
    └── current -> snapshots/snap-<utc>-<sha12>   # absolute symlink
```

Snapshot names are `snap-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha12>` so that reverse
lexicographic order *is* reverse chronological order — the GC needs no `stat`
calls and no name parsing.

### `STAMP` schema

A flat `key=value` file, one pair per line. It is **data, not code**: both scripts
parse it with a whitelist and validate each value (`keyhash` must be 64 lowercase
hex characters, `status ∈ {complete, partial}`, `sha` hex). Nothing in it is ever
`eval`ed or `source`d.

```
sha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>
keyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>
timestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>
timestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>
status=complete|partial
build_seconds=<integer>
toolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>
snapshot=<snapshot directory name>
warmer_version=1
```

## Core invariants (inherited from the parent workflow's post-mortems)

These encode incidents the parent repo paid for; violating them re-introduces
documented failure modes. Sources are cited in `local/protocols/*.md`.

1. **Single cache writer.** Only the warmer writes the hot main cache; agent
   worktrees consume copy-on-write clones and never write back. (GitHub's
   per-PR cache saves evicted the main entry: pr-ci.yml:138-142.)
2. **Review only after green CI, on the same head SHA.** The gate reads the
   exact-head `local-ci/*` statuses; a failed or absent CI summary blocks the
   review, which then publishes nothing at all — the *absence* of a green
   `local-review/summary` is the block, never a silent skip. Bot commits with prefix
   `[codex-auto-fix]`/`[codex-review-fix]` are not re-reviewed except the final
   fix at the iteration cap, which gets one forced review.
3. **Serialized fixes.** ci-fix → blueprint-fix → review-fix strictly in order,
   one branch at a time; combined iteration cap (default 5) across all fix
   kinds; sync/audit CI failures are never auto-fixed.
4. **Kill-switch semantics.** `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` and
   `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` disable only on the literal string `false`;
   unset means enabled.
5. **Trusted prompts.** Reviewer/fixer personas are read from committed `main`
   (`git show main:...`), never from the branch under review.
6. **Untrusted data framing.** Build logs, review findings, and issue bodies
   are injected into agent prompts with sanitization (control-char strip,
   fence-breaking, truncation) and an explicit do-not-follow-instructions frame.
7. **One full `lake build` machine-wide at a time** (advisory lock);
   single-file `lake env lean` checks need no lock.
8. **origin/main must resolve.** The hooks and diff-based audits silently
   self-disable without it; the local convention is a `main` branch plus a
   `refs/remotes/origin/main` alias maintained by `pr_merge.py`.
9. **Bracket-free naming.** Issue titles, slugs, and branch names avoid
   `]` and friends (broke the parent automation: CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124).
10. **Report-only stays report-only.** Stale-issue audit, linter sweep, README
    freshness never mutate state; write-mode is a separate human-invoked
    command.
11. **Faithfulness policy is unchanged.** AGENTS.md's faithful-formalization
    rules, anti-pattern catalog, and statement-integrity audits apply to QPBT
    exactly as to LDT.

## Naming and identity conventions

- **Issues and PRs**: GitHub's, identified by their numbers; sub-issues carry
  the parent/child structure and repository labels are the taxonomy
  (`issues-prs.md`). PR bodies keep the Motivation/Description/Testing shape of
  CONTRIBUTING.md; evidence is exact-head commit statuses, the manifest comment
  and the COMMENT review.
- **Branches**: `issue-<number>-<slug>` (orchestrator/human),
  `codex/issue-<number>-<slug>` (agent-created); the number is the GitHub
  issue's.
- **Fix commits**: `autofix.sh`'s subjects are prefixed `[codex-auto-fix]` /
  `[codex-review-fix]` exactly (the review-gate skip regex depends on them);
  operator and worker repairs use plain `fix(...)` subjects and are reviewed.
- **Agent sessions**: `<role>-<issue|scope>-<yyyymmdd>-<seq>` with roles
  `orc, prover, reviewer, simplifier, blueprint, splitter, scout`. Dispatched
  only via `local/bin/dispatch.sh`, which records the codex `thread_id`,
  captures the `--json` event stream to
  `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl`, and appends a summary line to
  `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`. Archiving a session = final status line
  in the registry + worktree removal; the JSONL capture is the archive.

## Telemetry (research-paper data)

All appends are one-line JSON; schemas documented in `protocols/meta.md`.

- `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` — one line per agent session: name, role,
  issue/pr, thread_id, start/end, wall seconds, token usage (input, cached,
  output, reasoning), exit status, dispatcher.
- `results/telemetry/stages.jsonl` — one line per project stage/substage
  transition with timestamps and manual token/agent tallies.
- `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` — one line per full build / cache event:
  kind (warm, rebuild, cache-get), duration, outcome, trigger.
- `results/telemetry/events.md` — dated free-form incident log (what broke,
  diagnosis, fix); the raw feed for `protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.
- `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` — dated protocol amendments: cause (cite an
  `events.md` entry or telemetry), the change, expected effect. This file is
  the primary record of workflow self-evolution.

- codex CLI (`gpt-5.6-sol`, ultra effort) drives orchestrator/prover/reviewer/

  reserved for hard reasoning (proof strategy, protocol synthesis, adversarial
  verification).
- Reviewer and prover roles must be **different sessions** — a session never
  reviews its own diff.

9. **Bracket-free naming.** Issue titles, slugs, and branch names avoid
   `]` and friends (broke the parent automation: CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124).
10. **Report-only stays report-only.** Stale-issue audit, linter sweep, README
    freshness never mutate state; write-mode is a separate human-invoked
    command.
11. **Faithfulness policy is unchanged.** AGENTS.md's faithful-formalization
    rules, anti-pattern catalog, and statement-integrity audits apply to QPBT
    exactly as to LDT.

## Naming and identity conventions

- **Issues and PRs**: GitHub's, identified by their numbers; sub-issues carry
  the parent/child structure and repository labels are the taxonomy
  (`issues-prs.md`). PR bodies keep the Motivation/Description/Testing shape of
  CONTRIBUTING.md; evidence is exact-head commit statuses, the manifest comment
  and the COMMENT review.
- **Branches**: `issue-<number>-<slug>` (orchestrator/human),
  `codex/issue-<number>-<slug>` (agent-created); the number is the GitHub
  issue's.
- **Fix commits**: `autofix.sh`'s subjects are prefixed `[codex-auto-fix]` /
  `[codex-review-fix]` exactly (the review-gate skip regex depends on them);
  operator and worker repairs use plain `fix(...)` subjects and are reviewed.
- **Agent sessions**: `<role>-<issue|scope>-<yyyymmdd>-<seq>` with roles
  `orc, prover, reviewer, simplifier, blueprint, splitter, scout`. Dispatched
  only via `local/bin/dispatch.sh`, which records the codex `thread_id`,
  captures the `--json` event stream to
  `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl`, and appends a summary line to
  `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`. Archiving a session = final status line
  in the registry + worktree removal; the JSONL capture is the archive.

## Telemetry (research-paper data)

All appends are one-line JSON; schemas documented in `protocols/meta.md`.

- `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` — one line per agent session: name, role,
  issue/pr, thread_id, start/end, wall seconds, token usage (input, cached,
  output, reasoning), exit status, dispatcher.
- `results/telemetry/stages.jsonl` — one line per project stage/substage
  transition with timestamps and manual token/agent tallies.
- `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` — one line per full build / cache event:
  kind (warm, rebuild, cache-get), duration, outcome, trigger.
- `results/telemetry/events.md` — dated free-form incident log (what broke,
  diagnosis, fix); the raw feed for `protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.
- `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` — dated protocol amendments: cause (cite an
  `events.md` entry or telemetry), the change, expected effect. This file is
  the primary record of workflow self-evolution.

## Model policy

- codex CLI (`gpt-5.6-sol`, ultra effort) drives orchestrator/prover/reviewer/
  simplifier sessions (`codex exec`, `codex exec review`).
- Claude-side subagents: easy/mechanical tasks run on Opus-tier; Fable-tier is
  reserved for hard reasoning (proof strategy, protocol synthesis, adversarial
  verification).
- Reviewer and prover roles must be **different sessions** — a session never
  reviews its own diff.

1	# Palomar preparation checker
     2	
     3	This directory contains a non-executing preparation check for the Palomar
     4	submission snapshot. It does not replace Palomar's official preparation and
     5	verification workflows.
     6	
     7	Run the focused fixtures:
     8	
     9	```sh
    10	python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/palomar/tests -v
    11	```
    12	
    13	Generate the deterministic report against the substantive repository's pinned
    14	revision (the path is read-only and is not written into the report):
    15	
    16	```sh
    17	python3 tools/palomar/check.py report \
    18	  --substantive-repo /path/to/MIPStarRE-QPBT \
    19	  --output reports/palomar-mechanical.json
    20	```
    21	
    22	`check` prints the same report without writing it. Both commands exit nonzero
    23	when a static requirement fails; `unknown` authoritative checks do not hide a
    24	static failure. The report hashes every wrapper input except its own output and
    25	binds the separately pinned Lean sources by Git tree and aggregate content
    26	hashes. It deliberately contains no wrapper commit SHA, so committing a
    27	regenerated report is not self-referential.
    28	
    29	Evidence classes are explicit:
    30	
    31	- `schema` validates `formalization.yaml` with the vendored official v0.4
    32	  schema snapshot.
    33	- `static` checks repository bytes, source text, Lake metadata, imports, and
    34	  comparator configuration. Static checks cannot certify a proof or an axiom
    35	  closure.
    36	- `authoritative` remains `unknown` until an official Palomar/comparator report
    37	  for the final integrated source snapshot is supplied and reviewed. A source
    38	  scan is never promoted to proof evidence.

    40	For an exact-head gate, pass the downloaded official report with
    41	`--official-report`. It is accepted only when it reports a completed pass for
    42	the current Git head, the configured wrapper repository, the four expected
    43	declarations, the standard axiom set, and protected `nanoda` and `con-ron`
    44	kernels.

     1	name: Comparator verification
     2	
     3	# Runs the official leanprover/comparator: the MIPStarRE-A library (pinned in
     4	# lakefile.toml and lake-manifest.json) proves exactly the statements in
     5	# Challenge.lean using only propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice, replayed
     6	# through the Lean kernel and the independent nanoda kernel.  The challenge
     7	# is Challenge.lean together with the modules under Challenge/.  See the
     8	# Validating Proofs chapter of the Lean reference manual for the trust model.
     9	#
    10	# The systemd-run guard from the comparator README is omitted: it hardens
    11	# against landrun escapes by untrusted solutions, and both modules here come
    12	# from this trusted checkout.
    13	#
    14	# This is the authoritative run.  On the development host the sandbox and the
    15	# external kernel are unavailable (no Go, no modern Rust), so local runs use
    16	# ./verify.sh --fake-landrun and are functional checks only.
    17	
    18	on:
    19	  push:
    20	    branches: [main, master, issue-662-closure-20260921-diagnostic]
    21	  pull_request:
    22	  workflow_dispatch:
    23	  schedule:
    24	    - cron: '41 5 * * 1'  # weekly: catch upstream tool or cache drift
    25	
    26	concurrency:
    27	  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
    28	  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    29	
    30	jobs:
    31	  comparator:
    32	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    33	    timeout-minutes: 360
    34	
    35	    steps:
    36	      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    37	
    38	      - name: Check the challenge imports only Mathlib and its own modules
    39	        run: |
    40	          # The challenge is one Mathlib-only module per contributing library
    41	          # module (see the README): every module may import Mathlib and other
    42	          # Challenge modules, and nothing else -- in particular never the
    43	          # library it is meant to be an independent statement of.

results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:2892:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: opus-bc57dd05-comparator-acceptance -->\nThe official Lean comparator (`leanprover/comparator`, pinned at v4.32.0) was run\nfor the first time end to end against the QPBT challenge on 2026-09-19\n(report `/tmp/meta-qpbt-comparator-verify-20260919.md`, packet K5).  The build,\nthe axiom criterion and a full `lean4checker` kernel replay of all 675 modules\nall pass, but the comparator **rejects** the pair:\n\n\u200b`\u200b`\u200b`\nuncaught exception: Const does not match between challenge and target\n                    'MIPStarRE.QPBT.qubitOperatorDistanceB'\n\u200b`\u200b`\u200b`\n\n## Cause\n\n`MIPStarRE.QPBT.QubitRegister P` unfolds to\n`Cube P.m \u00d7 Fin P.model.basisDim \u2192 ZMod 2`, so giving it a `Fintype` needs\n`@ZMod.fintype 2 _`, whose `NeZero` argument is a *proof*.  Lean abstracts a\nnon-trivial nested proof out of a definition's value into an auto-generated\nauxiliary constant, and names that constant after whichever declaration first\nneeded it.  That declaration is not the same in the two environments:\n\n| environment | auxiliary constant | statement | value |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| library (`Solution`) | `MIPStarRE.QPBT.idealQubitState._proof_2` | `NeZero (1 + 1)` | `@Nat.instNeZeroSucc 1` |\n| Mathlib-only `Challenge` | `MIPStarRE.QPBT.qubitPauliProj._proof_1` | `NeZero (1 + 1)` | `@Nat.instNeZeroSucc 1` |\n\nSame proposition, same proof term, different *name* \u2014 so\n`qubitOperatorDistanceA` and `qubitOperatorDistanceB` differ structurally and\nthe comparator stops at the first one it reaches.  This is not a soundness\nproblem; the kernel replay passes.\n\n## Work\n\nName every order-dependent auxiliary constant that appears in the QPBT\nstatement closure, so no `_proof_N` constant whose name depends on elaboration\norder survives in it.  This is the same class of repair as\n`fix(qpbt): name the Galois local instances in the closure`.\n\nAll changes must be statement-preserving: the statements of\n`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` and\n`MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one` stay byte-identical, no `sorry`, no new\naxiom, standard axioms only.\n\n## Acceptance\n\nA local comparator run in `/home/drx/QPBT-comparator` (branch `draft-challenge`,\n`./verify.sh --fake-landrun`) accepts the challenge/solution pair.",
results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:2921:  "title": "Comparator tooling: support more than one challenge",
results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:2966:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: opus-cd98bfab-comparator-multi -->\n### Motivation\n\nThe comparator challenge generator under `scripts/comparator/` is written for a\nsingle challenge: the extractor hard-codes the import of\n`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.MainTheorem.MainFormal` and the target\n`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal`, the assembler carries one global\n`EXTRAS`/`MODULE_PRELUDES` pair that hard-fails on any closure whose\ndeclarations do not match those LDT-only keys, and the drift check knows one\nexpected file.\n\nThe QPBT comparator work (scoping report of packet K0) needs a second challenge\ncovering three targets \u2014 `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness`,\n`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` and `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one`\n\u2014 with its own elaboration-context tables. The tooling must therefore become\nmulti-challenge before the QPBT challenge content can be developed.\n\n### Description\n\nIntroduce a per-challenge configuration file consumed by all three stages:\n\n- `scripts/comparator/challenges/*.json` \u2014 imports, target list, header/footer\n  paths, expected-file path, and the per-challenge `EXTRAS` / `MODULE_PRELUDES`\n  tables.\n- `extract_closure.lean` \u2014 closure of several targets, imports rendered per\n  challenge, deterministic dependency order.\n- `assemble_challenge.py` \u2014 per-challenge context tables instead of LDT-only\n  globals.\n- `check_challenge_drift.py` \u2014 checks every configured challenge whose expected\n  file exists and reports a clear skip when one does not.\n\n### Testing\n\n- `python3 -m unittest` over `scripts/tests/` (config loading, multi-target\n  ordering, absent expected file).\n- `python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root .` on a built\n  worktree: the LDT expected file must stay byte-identical.\n\n### Acceptance\n\n- `scripts/comparator/expected/Challenge.lean.expected` unchanged, LDT drift\n  check still green.\n- QPBT challenge configured but with no expected file committed yet; the drift\n  check skips it gracefully.",
results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:3052:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: opus-apache-licence-20260919 -->\nThe repository has no top-level licence file, so the code currently carries no\ngrant of rights at all.\n\nOwner decision (2026-09-19): \"use the license ldt uses. for the references, do\nwhat ldt does.\"\n\nWhat the companion LDT repositories do:\n\n- `LionSR/LDT-comparator` (the LDT challenge repository) is Apache-2.0.\n- `LionSR/MIPStarRE` (the LDT library repository) keeps its paper sources under\n  `references/ldt-paper` in the public repository with no separate notice.\n\nTherefore:\n\n1. Add a top-level `LICENSE` holding the Apache License 2.0, byte-identical to\n   the copy used by `LionSR/LDT-comparator`.\n2. Leave `references/` exactly as it is \u2014 the paper sources stay in the\n   repository, unchanged, as third-party material kept for reference.\n\nScope is deliberately narrow: a new `LICENSE` file, plus the README licence\nsection only if the README carries a placeholder line for it.",
results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:3081:  "title": "Comparator challenge for the QPBT headline theorems: tooling and environment alignment",
results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:3126:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: comparator-challenge-for-the-qpbt-headline-theorems-tooling-7e17e7e2 -->\nThe LDT headline theorem `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` is already covered by\na comparator challenge (`docs/comparator.md`, `scripts/comparator/`, companion\nrepository `LDT-comparator`).  The QPBT headline theorems have no such\ncoverage.\n\nThis issue tracks giving `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` and\n`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` the same treatment:\n\n1. **Tooling parameterization.**  `scripts/comparator/` is currently\n   single-challenge: the extractor hard-codes the LDT root, and the assembler's\n   elaboration-context tables are LDT-specific.  Introduce a per-challenge\n   configuration (target theorem names, header, footer, expected file path,\n   context tables) without changing the LDT outputs by a single byte \u2014\n   `check_challenge_drift.py` must still pass for LDT.\n2. **Closure extraction.**  Produce\n   `scripts/comparator/expected/ChallengeQPBT.lean.expected`: a Mathlib-only\n   file that re-declares every declaration of the comparator-relevant statement\n   closure of the two QPBT targets verbatim and in dependency order, then states\n   both theorems with `sorry`.\n3. **Environment alignment.**  Every module contributing a declaration to the\n   QPBT closure must see the full `import Mathlib` (directly or through an\n   existing base module), carrying the same \"do not narrow this import\"\n   comment, so the challenge file elaborates to terms identical to the\n   library's.  Verbatim-redeclaration obstacles (custom notation, local\n   instances, private or auxiliary declarations, `open ... in`, attribute side\n   effects) are resolved with the smallest faithful edits \u2014 no statement and no\n   proof term of a headline theorem changes.\n4. **Documentation and CI.**  A QPBT section in `docs/comparator.md` and a QPBT\n   drift check next to the LDT one in `pr-ci.yml`.\n\nThe challenge repository itself is\n<https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator>; its `draft-challenge` branch\nreceives `Challenge.lean`, `Solution.lean`, `lakefile.toml`, `comparator.json`\nand `verify.sh`, with the library pinned by commit.\n\nConstraints: no `sorry`/`admit`/`axiom` enters the library, the statements of\n`pauli_soundness` and `pauli_soundness_qubit` stay byte-identical, and the\naxiom closure stays `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.",
results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:3200:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: opus-blueprint-final-20260919 -->\nArtifact packet A-BLUEPRINT. The blueprint graph must be truthful before the\nrepository is attached as an artifact to an ITP submission: a reader who opens\nthe dependency graph and sees the main theorem unmarked concludes it is\nunproved.\n\nScope (blueprint/ only, no Lean change):\n\n1. Recompute, on current `github/main`, every node of QPBT chapters 11-16 that\n   lacks a statement-level or a proof-level `\\leanok`. Two earlier helpers\n   disagreed about what is still missing, so nothing is taken on trust.\n2. Classify each such node as (a) should be marked \u2014 the Lean declarations\n   exist, are sorry-free, and depend only on the standard axioms, verified with\n   `#print axioms`; (b) correctly unmarked, with the reason stated; or (c)\n   needing an explicit exemption remark.\n3. Add the marks the convention in `AGENTS.md` and\n   `docs/blueprint_style_guide.md` allows; for correctly unmarked source-shape\n   nodes add a one-line remark pointing at the corrected node, so no unmarked\n   node is left unexplained.\n4. Rebuild the blueprint locally to confirm the source still builds.\n5. `scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py --ci` must exit 0.\n\nDefinition of done: final counts reported for nodes, statement-level marks,\nproof-bearing nodes, proof-level marks and exemptions; no statement or\ndefinition altered; proof integrity rules of `AGENTS.md` respected.",
results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:3274:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: opus-gap-notes-build-20260919 -->\nThe reviewer-facing justification for every statement correction lives in\n`docs/paper-gaps/*.tex`, but the directory has no build target and no evidence\nthat the notes compile. The only build path is the external `texra-blueprint`\ntool, which a reviewer does not have.\n\nFor the ITP artifact the directory needs:\n\n1. a `docs/paper-gaps/Makefile` with `all`, `clean` and `check` targets that\n   build every note with `latexmk` into an ignored `docs/paper-gaps/build/`,\n   where `check` fails on any LaTeX error or undefined reference;\n2. every note to actually compile, with compile errors, undefined references\n   and broken labels repaired by the smallest edits that change no mathematical\n   content and no statement;\n3. a `docs/paper-gaps/README.md` explaining how to build, with one line per\n   note (title, paper locator, status), pointing at `qpbt-gap-register.md` and\n   `docs/DEVIATIONS.md`.\n\nNo PDFs are committed; the artifact packaging step builds them at release time.\n\nSource: the ITP submission-readiness audit of 2026-09-19, section 3 (\"the gap\nnotes do not build\") and to-do item 10.",
results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:3348:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: opus-artifact-packaging-20260919 -->\nThe repository is to be attached as an **artifact** to an ITP submission. The\nacting-main design decision (2026-09-19) is that the artifact is a **release\nsnapshot of the mathematical development**, produced by a script from a tagged\ncommit \u2014 not the whole working repository.\n\nExcluded from the snapshot (kept in the repository for research purposes):\n\n- the AI-workflow layer: `results/telemetry/`, `local/`, `.github/` prompts,\n  `.githooks/`, and scripts that only serve the workflow;\n- the third-party paper mirrors under `references/`, until the owner decides\n  about redistribution (ITP-readiness audit section 5). The snapshot's docs\n  cite the papers by arXiv identifier and record which commit of which file the\n  docstring locators refer to.\n\nExcluding the workflow layer also removes the 2,456 tracked files that mention\nthe developer's home path from the artifact, without rewriting history\n(readiness to-do item 13).\n\nDeliverables:\n\n1. `scripts/make_artifact.sh <git-ref> <out-dir>` \u2014 `git archive` driven by\n   `export-ignore` attributes, builds the gap-note PDFs when\n   `docs/paper-gaps/Makefile` exists (degrades gracefully when it does not),\n   writes a MANIFEST (source commit, file count, Lean code-line total,\n   toolchain, Mathlib revision), runs a leak scan that fails the script on a\n   hit unless whitelisted with a reason, prints the tarball name and sha256,\n   and offers `--anonymize` for a possible double-blind venue.\n2. `docs/ARTIFACT.md` \u2014 what the artifact contains and excludes and why, the\n   exact verification steps for a reviewer, and the maintainers' release\n   procedure.\n3. `.gitattributes` `export-ignore` lines and a unit-style smoke test under\n   `scripts/tests/`.\n\nRelated readiness to-do items: 11 (clean-clone build, scheduled separately),\n13 (home-path scrub, solved by exclusion), 15 (whether telemetry ships,\nanswered: it does not), 17 (anonymized snapshot, covered by `--anonymize`).",
results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:3496:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: qpbt-axiom-audit-ci-20260919 -->\nThe ITP-readiness audit (2026-09-19, section 2) records that the axiom-cleanliness\nclaim for QPBT is **not reproducible inside the repository**: there are zero\n`#print axioms` directives in the QPBT tree, and the only audit module,\n`MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean`, covers LDT only. The \"three standard\naxioms\" result came from a one-off metaprogram in a discarded worktree, so a\nreviewer cannot re-run it.\n\nSeparately, audit section 1 records that `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml` builds\n`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit` only, so no CI job ever builds a QPBT axiom\naudit target.\n\nScope of this issue:\n\n1. Add `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean` using the same elaboration-time\n   mechanism as the LDT audit (`assert_standard_axioms`, which calls\n   `Lean.collectAxioms` and throws unless the axiom set is exactly\n   `{propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}`), plus a printing pass so the\n   axioms are visible in the build log. The file fails to compile if a\n   headline theorem picks up `sorryAx` or any other axiom.\n2. Cover the QPBT headline theorems named in the end-state report section 2,\n   including the two corrected forms `exists_extendedLinesWitness_established`\n   and `exists_symmetric_projective_strategy_approx`.\n3. Wire the module into CI (`local/bin/ci.sh` build step and the GitHub\n   workflow) the way the LDT audit is wired, so an axiom regression fails CI.\n\nTrigger: owner policy decision 2026-09-19 that completion requires a\ncaveat-free, comparator-checked formalization ready to attach as an ITP\nartifact.",
results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:3570:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: readme-for-the-qpbt-artifact-f312dbff -->\nThe repository README still describes the inherited LDT track. It never names\nthe quantum Pauli basis test, its headline theorems, the build commands for\n`MIPStarRE.QPBT`, or the artifact status, and its layout block advertises two\ntop-level directories (`issues/`, `prs/`) that do not exist on `github/main`.\n\nRewrite `README.md` (that file only) so a sceptical ITP reviewer who clones the\nrepository learns, within two screens:\n\n- what is formalized: the quantum Pauli basis test of the MIP*=RE paper, with\n  the headline theorem names and file paths, and the LDT development it builds on;\n- the status: zero `sorry`, standard Lean axioms only, documented statement\n  corrections where the source paper's printed claims are not established;\n- how to build and check: toolchain, `lake exe cache get`, `lake build\n  MIPStarRE.QPBT`, the QPBT axiom-audit file, the comparator challenge\n  repository, and build times/machine requirements taken from recorded evidence\n  in `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` rather than guessed;\n- the repository layout as it really is, including an honest note that `local/`\n  and `results/telemetry/` document the AI-assisted workflow and are not part of\n  the mathematical artifact;\n- where to read more, linking the artifact documents that parallel packets are\n  adding under `docs/`.\n\nLicence: a one-line placeholder only; the owner has not chosen a licence yet.\n\nScope: `README.md` only. Documentation change, no Lean edits.",
results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:3644:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: qpbt-theorem-index-20260919 -->\nArtifact packet A-INDEX: the repository has no reviewer-facing index of what is\nproved. The mapping paper statement -> Lean declaration -> file:line -> blueprint\nnode -> axioms exists only outside the repository and will be lost.\n\nDeliverable: a single new file `docs/QPBT-theorem-index.md` covering the results\nof the paper's Pauli basis test section and the chain they rest on:\n\n- the headline soundness theorems `pauli_soundness` and `pauli_soundness_qubit`;\n- the quantum low-degree soundness they use;\n- the main combining, observables and extraction theorems;\n- the commutation / anticommutation tests;\n- the key definitions: the game, strategies, value, the error function\n  `deltaQld`, admissible parameters.\n\nEach row carries: paper locator (file and line range under `references/qpbt-paper`,\ntheorem/lemma label), an informal one-sentence statement, the fully qualified Lean\ndeclaration with file:line on `github/main`, the blueprint node label, the axioms\nprinted by `#print axioms`, and a \"differs from the paper?\" column.\n\nAlso: a section listing the two printed claims recorded as non-asserted `Props`\n(from PRs 633 and 634) together with their proved corrected forms; the commit hash\nthe index was generated from; and the command to regenerate the axioms column.\n\nEverything verified against the tree, nothing guessed. Docs only - no Lean source\nfile changes.\n\nContext: ITP submission-readiness audit 2026-09-19, section 2 and to-do item 5.",

results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:3866:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: completion-protocol-definition-of-done-with-zero-caveats-fc2a57b9 -->\nThe workflow has no written definition of \"finished\". Every gate we run today\nanswers a local question (does this PR build, is this blueprint node marked, is\nthis note well formed); nothing answers the project-level question the owner\nasked on 2026-09-19:\n\n> some protocol(s) in the workflow should ensure that when the project\n> finishes, the formalization is done without caveat, and satisfies the lean\n> comparator.\n\nand, earlier the same day, \"i want zero sorry\".\n\nWithout such a definition the failure mode is predictable: a track gets\ndeclared done while a paper-gap row still says \"open\", a blueprint node is\nunmarked, or the comparator challenge lags the library commit that is being\nannounced.\n\n## Deliverables\n\n1. `local/protocols/completion.md` \u2014 normative \"Definition of done\" for a\n   formalization track, with a per-track headline-theorem table (QPBT first),\n   the six criteria that make \"finished without caveat\" mean something, and\n   who enforces them.\n2. `scripts/completion_gate.py` \u2014 model-free, stdlib-only checker\n   (`check --track qpbt`) printing PASS/FAIL per criterion with file:line\n   evidence, exit 0 only when every mechanically checkable criterion passes.\n3. Unit tests under `scripts/tests/` with fixture trees per criterion.\n4. Pointers from `local/personas/main.md` and `local/README.md`, and the\n   `EVOLUTION.md` entry required by `local/protocols/meta.md`.\n\n## Expected state on delivery\n\nThe gate is expected to FAIL today: QPBT has no comparator challenge, the\npaper-gap register has no terminal-status column, and the QPBT axiom audit\nfile does not exist. That is the point \u2014 the gate's output is the remaining\nto-do list, not a blocker.\n\nThe gate is deliberately NOT added to the blocking PR CI.\n\n## Owner decision needed (separate)\n\nWhere the QPBT comparator challenge repository lives is the one part of this\nthat leaves the repository; it is raised with the owner separately.",

results/telemetry/events.md:9339:- 2026-09-19T12:49:41Z OPUS-BUILD completion protocol (#635): the workflow had no written definition of "finished". Every gate answered a per-PR question; nothing answered the owner's 2026-09-19 policy question, that when the project finishes the formalization is done without caveat and satisfies the Lean comparator. Diagnosis: the failure mode is a completion statement posted while a paper-gap row still says "open", a blueprint node is unmarked, or the comparator pin lags the announced commit — none of which any existing check looks at. Fix: `local/protocols/completion.md` plus the model-free `scripts/completion_gate.py`, which main must run and attach before any completion statement, issue closure or release tag. First real run on c6c8c2f2 exits 1: C1 (no sorry/admit/axiom/native site under `MIPStarRE/QPBT`) and C6 pass, C2 (no QPBT `AxiomAudit.lean`), C3 (register has no terminal-status column), C4 (8 of 515 linked blueprint nodes unmarked) and C5 (no comparator challenge for QPBT) fail. Lesson: the gate found two false positives of the imported `DECL_RE` on continuation lines opening with the local name `constant`, so an imported rule still needs its own evidence read before it is trusted at a new tree; and zero sorry sites is now a fact about main, not an aspiration — it was never checked as such before. Second review round on the same PR found the one hole left: C5 decided its coverage clause from `covered-theorems`, a list hand-written in `docs/comparator.md` by the same session that would declare the track finished, and never read the expected challenge it had already located — a document validating itself. C5 now takes the expected-copy path from the track registry, requires the record to name exactly that copy, and requires every headline theorem to occur in it by its fully-qualified name; a seventh criterion, artifact readiness, checks fail-closed that the files an ITP artifact submission needs (`README.md`, `docs/QPBT-theorem-index.md`, `docs/DEVIATIONS.md`, `docs/ARTIFACT.md`, `LICENSE`, `scripts/make_artifact.sh`) are committed, with the snapshot's leak scan delegated like the other run-dependent halves. Lesson: a criterion whose evidence is written in the document it judges is not a check, and "done" now includes being attachable as an artifact, per the owner's 2026-09-19 policy. Refreshing onto main during the fix also showed C2 reporting all four headline theorems uncovered against the QPBT audit module main had just merged: that module defines its own command `audit_standard_axioms` beside the LDT `assert_standard_axioms`, so the gate now accepts either. Second lesson: a gate that names one tree's spelling of a shared practice goes stale the moment another tree adopts the practice.

A member that moved makes the lease stale, and git 2.34's `reject_atomic_push` aborts the whole transaction client-side before any ref is sent, so `main` is not published either; a member that did not move is up to date and is never rewound. `test_member_moving_at_transport_start_refuses` (`scripts/tests/test_pr_train.py:268-292`) is a real end-to-end exercise of this: a `git` shim moves `refs/heads/issue-3` on the fixture remote at the moment the push starts, and the test asserts non-zero exit, remote `main` still at base, the member keeping its racing value, \\\"rejected\\\" on stderr, `publication.json` outcome `refused`, and no non-GET GitHub call. The new `EXIT` trap at `checked-push.sh:154` clobbers no earlier trap (there is none).\\n\\nF2 (`pr_train.py:171`, private telemetry lock). `record()` now writes through `telemetry.append_jsonl` and `telemetry.append_event_bullet` (`pr_train.py:181-204`); `telemetry.py:478-485` takes the canonical `events-md` named lock and the dated-section path, so a concurrent canonical writer can no longer truncate or lose the train event. An unreadable build spool is kept for the operator rather than deleted.\\n\\nChecked beyond the ledger. `ci.sh --integration-head` sets `FORCE_ALL=1`, rejects `--only`/`--skip-build`/a PR argument, requires 40-hex head and base plus `--worktree`, and re-asserts head identity, cleanliness and base ancestry before and after the run; because `--base` is set the run is `PARTIAL=1`, so it publishes no statuses, no summary and no manifest comment, and its manifest lands at `pr<PR_ID>-<sha>.partial.json`, which is exactly the path `pr_train.ci_path` reads. `check_combined_ci` re-reads that manifest and requires head, merge base, worktree, conclusion and every one of `pr_merge.CI_STEPS` to be `success` with no extra or missing step, so a partial manifest cannot certify a subset. do\n  case \"${1:-}\" in\n    --repo-root) [ \"$#\" -ge 2 ] || die \"--repo-root requires a path\"; REPO_ROOT=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n    --train-manifest) [ \"$#\" -ge 2 ] || die \"--train-manifest requires a path\"; TRAIN_MANIFEST=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n    *) break ;;\n  esac\ndone\n\ncase \"${1:-}\" in\n  --help|-h)\n    usage\n    exit 0\n    ;;\nesac\n[ \"$#\" -eq 2 ] || { usage >&2; exit 2; }\n\nREMOTE=\"$1\"\nREFSPEC=\"$2\"\ncase \"$REMOTE\" in\n  \"\"|-*) die \"REMOTE must name a configured Git remote\" ;;\nesac\n\nLOCAL_REF=\"${REFSPEC%%:*}\"\nREMOTE_REF=\"${REFSPEC#*:}\"\nif [ \"$LOCAL_REF\" = \"$REFSPEC\" ]; then\n  die \"refspec must map an explicit local branch to an explicit remote branch\"\nfi\ncase \"$LOCAL_REF:$REMOTE_REF\" in\n  refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*) ;;\n  *) die \"both sides of the refspec must start with refs/heads/\" ;;\nesac\n\nREPO_ROOT=\"$(git -C \"$REPO_ROOT\" rev-parse --show-toplevel)\" ||\n  die \"cannot resolve repository root from $REPO_ROOT\"\ngit -C \"$REPO_ROOT\" check-ref-format \"$LOCAL_REF\" >/dev/null ||\n  die \"invalid local ref $LOCAL_REF\"\ngit -C \"$REPO_ROOT\" check-ref-format \"$REMOTE_REF\" >/dev/null ||\n  die \"invalid remote ref $REMOTE_REF\"\n\nif [ \"${MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS:-}\" = \"1\" ]; then\n  [ -z \"$TRAIN_MANIFEST\" ] || die \"a train cannot bypass checked publication\"\n  unset MIPSTARRE_EXPECTED_PUSH_TUPLE\n  # The bypass skips validation, not the explicit one-ref publication boundary.\n  exec git -C \"$REPO_ROOT\" -c push.followTags=false push --no-follow-tags \\\n    \"$REMOTE\" \"$REFSPEC\"\nfi\n\nLOCAL_SHA=\"$(git -C \"$REPO_ROOT\" rev-parse --verify \"$LOCAL_REF^{commit}\")\" ||\n  die \"cannot resolve local branch $LOCAL_REF\"\nWORKTREE_ROWS=\"$(git -C \"$REPO_ROOT\" worktree list --porcelain)\" ||\n  die \"cannot list registered worktrees\"\nVALIDATION_ROOT=\"\"\ncandidate=\"\"\nwhile IFS= read -r line; do\n  case \"$line\" in\n    \"worktree \"*) candidate=\"${line#worktree }\" ;;\n    \"branch $LOCAL_REF\") VALIDATION_ROOT=\"$candidate\"; break ;;\n  esac\ndone <<< \"$WORKTREE_ROWS\"\n[ -n \"$VALIDATION_ROOT\" ] ||\n  die \"$LOCAL_REF is not checked out in a registered worktree\"\nVALIDATION_ROOT=\"$(git -C \"$VALIDATION_ROOT\" rev-parse --show-toplevel)\" ||\n  die \"cannot resolve worktree for $LOCAL_REF\"\nrequire_validation_checkout\n\nREMOTE_URL=\"$(git -C \"$REPO_ROOT\" remote get-url --push \"$REMOTE\")\" ||\n  die \"cannot resolve push URL for remote $REMOTE\"\nREMOTE_ROWS=\"$(git -C \"$REPO_ROOT\" ls-remote --refs \"$REMOTE_URL\" \"$REMOTE_REF\")\" ||\n  die \"cannot read $REMOTE_REF from remote $REMOTE\"\n\nREMOTE_SHA=\"\"\nwhile IFS=$'\\t' read -r sha ref extra; do\n  [ -n \"$sha\" ] || continue\n  [ \"$ref\" = \"$REMOTE_REF\" ] || continue\n  [ -z \"$extra\" ] || die \"unexpected ls-remote output for $REMOTE_REF\"\n  [ -z \"$REMOTE_SHA\" ] || die \"remote $REMOTE returned $REMOTE_REF more than once\"\n  REMOTE_SHA=\"$sha\"\ndone <<< \"$REMOTE_ROWS\"\n[ -n \"$REMOTE_SHA\" ] || REMOTE_SHA=\"$ZERO_SHA\"\n[[ \"$LOCAL_SHA\" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || die \"unexpected local object id $LOCAL_SHA\"\n[[ \"$REMOTE_SHA\" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || die \"unexpected remote object id $REMOTE_SHA\"\nif [ \"$REMOTE_SHA\" != \"$ZERO_SHA\" ] &&\n    ! git -C \"$REPO_ROOT\" merge-base --is-ancestor \"$REMOTE_SHA\" \"$LOCAL_SHA\"; then\n  die \"$LOCAL_SHA would not fast-forward $REMOTE_REF from $REMOTE_SHA\"\nfi\n\nHOOK=\"$VALIDATION_ROOT/.githooks/pre-push\"\n[ -x \"$HOOK\" ] || die \"$HOOK is missing or not executable; run scripts/install_git_hooks.sh\"\n\n(\n  unset MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS\n  unset MIPSTARRE_EXPECTED_PUSH_TUPLE\n  cd \"$VALIDATION_ROOT\"\n  \"$HOOK\" \"$REMOTE\" \"$REMOTE_URL\"\n) <<< \"$LOCAL_REF $LOCAL_SHA $REMOTE_REF $REMOTE_SHA\"\n\nCURRENT_LOCAL_SHA=\"$(git -C \"$REPO_ROOT\" rev-parse --verify \"$LOCAL_REF^{commit}\")\" ||\n  die \"cannot re-resolve local branch $LOCAL_REF after preflight\"\n[ \"$CURRENT_LOCAL_SHA\" = \"$LOCAL_SHA\" ] ||\n  die \"local branch $LOCAL_REF changed during preflight\"\nrequire_validation_checkout\n\nMEMBER_LEASES=()\nMEMBER_SPECS=()\nif [ -n \"$TRAIN_MANIFEST\" ]; then\n  # The verifier reports the member refs it just confirmed; each one is leased\n  # below so the remote itself refuses the publication when a member branch\n  # moves between verification and the transport.\n  MEMBER_FILE=\"$(mktemp)\" || die \"cannot create a temporary file for the member refs\"\n  trap 'rm -f \"$MEMBER_FILE\"' EXIT\n  python3 \"$SCRIPT_ROOT/local/bin/pr_train.py\" --verify-manifest \"$TRAIN_MANIFEST\" \\\n    --expected-main \"$REMOTE_SHA\" --expected-head \"$LOCAL_SHA\" \\\n    --expected-ref \"$REMOTE_REF\" --members-out \"$MEMBER_FILE\" ||\n    die \"train changed during preflight\"\n  while IFS=' ' read -r member_ref member_sha extra; do\n    [ -n \"$member_ref\" ] || continue\n    [ -z \"$extra\" ] || die \"unexpected member row for $member_ref\"\n    case \"$member_ref\" in\n      refs/heads/*) ;;\n      *) die \"member ref $member_ref must start with refs/heads/\" ;;\n    esac\n    [ \"$member_ref\" != \"$REMOTE_REF\" ] ||\n      die \"member ref $member_ref collides with the published ref\"\n    git -C \"$REPO_ROOT\" check-ref-format \"$member_ref\" >/dev/null ||\n      die \"invalid member ref $member_ref\"\n    [[ \"$member_sha\" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] ||\n      die \"unexpected member object id $member_sha for $member_ref\"\n    for seen in ${MEMBER_SPECS[@]+\"${MEMBER_SPECS[@]}\"}; do\n      [ \"${seen#*:}\" != \"$member_ref\" ] || die \"member ref $member_ref appears twice\"\n    done\n    MEMBER_LEASES+=(\"--force-with-lease=$member_ref:$member_sha\")\n    MEMBER_SPECS+=(\"$member_sha:$member_ref\")\n  done < \"$MEMBER_FILE\"\n  [ \"${#MEMBER_SPECS[@]}\" -ge 2 ] ||\n    die \"train manifest verified fewer than two member refs\"\nfi\n\nprintf '%s: gate passed before opening the push transport.\\n' \"$PROG\" >&2\n# Freeze the source object and atomically require the preflight remote tip.  The\n# native hook is only a short defense-in-depth confirmation; the lease keeps the\n# tuple binding intact when that hook is stale or not selected.  A train adds one\n# no-op update per member ref under the same atomic transaction: each member is\n# pushed back at its verified value, so the remote compares the advertised value\n# at transport start and rejects the whole push -- main included -- when a member\n# moved, while a member that did not move is simply already up to date and stays\n# out of both the transaction and the native hook's tuple.  Disable implicit\n# annotated-tag expansion so the transport contains only the validated refs.\nLEASE_SHA=\"$REMOTE_SHA\"\n[ \"$LEASE_SHA\" != \"$ZERO_SHA\" ] || LEASE_SHA=\"\"\nMIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1 \\\n  MIPSTARRE_EXPECTED_PUSH_TUPLE=\"$LOCAL_SHA $LOCAL_SHA $REMOTE_REF $REMOTE_SHA\" \\\n  git -C \"$REPO_ROOT\" -c push.followTags=false push --no-follow-tags --atomic \\\n    --force-with-lease=\"$REMOTE_REF:$LEASE_SHA\" \\\n    ${MEMBER_LEASES[@]+\"${MEMBER_LEASES[@]}\"} \\\n    \"$REMOTE\" \"$LOCAL_SHA:$REMOTE_REF\" ${MEMBER_SPECS[@]+\"${MEMBER_SPECS[@]}\"}\n"}, "84a6bad9f6db3975681800ae18dede7cd8d938b9df37e66e7c4a09834096a9bf": {"encoding": "utf8", "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Integrate independently reviewed PR heads, check the result, and publish it.\n\nOperator-only after deployment. "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\nr\"\"\"\nTelemetry writer for the local operations layer.\n\nEvery append to ``results/telemetry/*`` goes through this script so the\nresearch-data invariants of ``local/protocols/meta.md`` hold: one JSON object\nper line, ISO-8601 timestamps with offset, locked appends (concurrent\nsessions), and idempotent re-runs.\n\nSubcommands::\n\n    telemetry.py session-summarize CAPTURE.jsonl [--name N] [--role R] ...\n    telemetry.py session-status --name N --status archived [--note TEXT]\n    telemetry.py stage --stage 4.3-proofs --event start [--note TEXT]\n    telemetry.py build --kind warm --outcome success --seconds 812\n    telemetry.py event --text \"symptom -> diagnosis -> fix -> lesson\"\n\n``session-summarize`` is the one that does real work: it reads a captured\n``codex exec --json`` event stream (JSONL on stdout: ``thread.started``,\n``turn.completed``, ``item.completed``) and emits the ``sessions.jsonl``\nregistry line described in ``local/DESIGN.md`` (\"Agent sessions\") and\n``local/protocols/meta.md`` (\"Telemetry duties\").  It replaces the parent\nrepository's GitHub-side accounting, where session identity came from a bot\ntoken and run metadata came from the Actions API; locally the codex\n``thread_id`` is the only session handle and it exists *only* in the event\nstream, so losing the capture loses the session (see\n``local/protocols/sessions.md``).\n\nThis script is stdlib-only and safe to call from several processes at once.\nIt never starts an agent: ``local/bin/dispatch.sh`` does that and calls this.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport fcntl\nimport json\nimport os\nimport re\nimport shlex\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any, Iterator, Sequence\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Layout\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n# local/bin/telemetry.py -> repository root\nREPO_ROOT_DEFAULT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]\n\nTELEMETRY_SUBDIR = Path(\"results\") / \"telemetry\"\n\n# Timestamp shape already used by results/telemetry/*.jsonl and by\n# `date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z` in the shell scripts.\nTS_FMT = \"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z\"\n\n# codex `turn.completed` usage keys -> meta.md `usage` schema keys.\nUSAGE_MAP = {\n    \"input_tokens\": \"input\",\n    \"cached_input_tokens\": \"cached_input\",\n    \"cache_write_input_tokens\": \"cache_write\",\n    \"output_tokens\": \"output\",\n    \"reasoning_output_tokens\": \"reasoning\",\n}\nUSAGE_KEYS = list(USAGE_MAP.values())\n\n# Documented vocabularies (meta.md).  Unknown values are written anyway but\n# warned about: refusing them would let a peer script lose telemetry entirely,\n# which is the worse failure.\nKNOWN_STAGES = (\n    \"1-skeleton\",\n    \"2-references\",\n    \"3-blueprint\",\n    \"4.1-minimal\",\n    \"4.2-full-skeleton\",\n    \"4.3-proofs\",\n)\nKNOWN_BUILD_KINDS = (\"warm\", \"rebuild\", \"cache-get\", \"ci-build\")\nKNOWN_OUTCOMES = (\"success\", \"failed\", \"partial\", \"skipped\")\nKNOWN_STATUSES = (\"active\", \"done\", \"failed\", \"archived\")\nROLES = (\n    \"orc\",\n    \"prover\",\n    \"reviewer\",\n    \"simplifier\",\n    \"blueprint\",\n    \"splitter\",\n    \"scout\",\n    \"mathfix\",\n)\n\nTOKEN_RE = re.compile(r\"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$\")\n\nEVENTS_HEADER = \"\"\"# Incident and observation log\n\nDated bullets, one incident each: symptom → diagnosis → fix → lesson.\nThis file is the raw feed for `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef warn(message: str) -> None:\n    sys.stderr.write(f\"telemetry.py: warning: {message}\\n\")\n\n\ndef fail(message: str, code: int = 4) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Abort with a diagnosis on stderr.  Never returns.\"\"\"\n    sys.stderr.write(f\"telemetry.py: error: {message}\\n\")\n    raise SystemExit(code)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Time\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef now_ts() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Current local time, ISO-8601 with numeric offset.\"\"\"\n    return datetime.now().astimezone().strftime(TS_FMT)\n\n\ndef parse_ts(text: str | None) -> datetime | None:\n    \"\"\"Parse an ISO-8601 timestamp and reject timezone-naive values.\"\"\"\n    if not text:\n        return None\n    text = text.strip()\n    if text.endswith(\"Z\"):\n        text = text[:-1] + \"+00:00\"\n    for fmt in (TS_FMT, \"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f%z\"):\n        try:\n            parsed = datetime.strptime(text, fmt)\n            return parsed if parsed.tzinfo is not None else None\n        except ValueError:\n            pass\n    try:\n        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(text)\n        return parsed if parsed.tzinfo is not None else None\n    except ValueError:\n        return None\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Runtime state and locking\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef cache_dir() -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Runtime state root.  Never inside the repository (DESIGN.md, Layout).\"\"\"\n    override = os.environ.get(\"MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT\")\n    if override:\n        return Path(override).expanduser()\n    return Path.home() / \".cache\" / \"mipstarre-dev\"\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef named_lock(name: str) -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Advisory lock held on a file under ``~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/``.\"\"\"\n    lock_dir = cache_dir() / \"locks\"\n    lock_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    lock_path = lock_dir / f\"{name}.lock\"\n    with open(lock_path, \"a+\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)\n        try:\n            yield\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n\n\ndef append_jsonl(path: Path, record: dict[str, Any]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Append one JSON object to ``path`` under an exclusive lock on the file.\"\"\"\n    line = json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False)\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o644)\n    with os.fdopen(fd, \"r+\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)\n        try:\n            _ensure_trailing_newline(handle)\n            handle.write(line + \"\\n\")\n            handle.flush()\n            os.fsync(handle.fileno())\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n    return line\n\n\ndef _ensure_trailing_newline(handle: Any) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Guard against a previous writer that died mid-line.\"\"\"\n    handle.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)\n    if handle.tell() == 0:\n        return\n    handle.seek(handle.tell() - 1)\n    if handle.read(1) != \"\\n\":\n        handle.write(\"\\n\")\n    handle.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)\n\n\ndef read_jsonl(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], int]:\n    \"\"\"Read a JSONL file, returning (objects, malformed line count).\"\"\"\n    if not path.exists():\n        return [], 0\n    objects: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n    errors = 0\n    for raw in path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\").splitlines():\n        raw = raw.strip()\n        if not raw:\n            continue\n        try:\n            obj = json.loads(raw)\n        except json.JSONDecodeError:\n            errors += 1\n            continue\n        if isinstance(obj, dict):\n            objects.append(obj)\n        else:\n            errors += 1\n    return objects, errors\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# codex event-stream parsing\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef deep_find(node: Any, keys: Sequence[str], depth: int = 0) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"First string value stored under any of ``keys``, searched breadth-first.\"\"\"\n    if depth > 8:\n        return None\n    if isinstance(node, dict):\n        for key in keys:\n            value = node.get(key)\n            if isinstance(value, str) and value:\n                return value\n        for value in node.values():\n            found = deep_find(value, keys, depth + 1)\n            if found:\n                return found\n    elif isinstance(node, list):\n        for value in node:\n            found = deep_find(value, keys, depth + 1)\n            if found:\n                return found\n    return None\n\n\ndef extract_thread_id(events: Sequence[dict[str, Any]]) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"codex session handle, needed for ``codex exec resume``.\n\n    Primary source is the ``thread.started`` event; the fallbacks exist because\n    a crashed run can truncate the stream before that event is flushed, and a\n    session with no recoverable id must be reported (never silently nulled).\n    \"\"\"\n    for event in events:\n        if event.get(\"type\") == \"thread.started\":\n            thread = event.get(\"thread\")\n            candidate = event.get(\"thread_id\")\n            if not isinstance(candidate, str) or not candidate:\n                candidate = thread.get(\"id\") if isinstance(thread, dict) else None\n            if isinstance(candidate, str) and candidate:\n                return candidate\n    for event in events:\n        found = deep_find(event, (\"thread_id\", \"conversation_id\", \"session_id\"))\n        if found:\n            return found\n    return None\n\n\ndef summarize_usage(\n    events: Sequence[dict[str, Any]], mode: str = \"sum\"\n) -> tuple[dict[str, int], int]:\n    \"\"\"Token usage over ``turn.completed`` events, normalized to meta.md keys.\n\n    ``mode=sum`` treats each turn's usage as a delta (codex 0.147.0 behaviour);\n    ``mode=last`` keeps only the final turn, for a codex build that ever starts\n    reporting cumulative counters.  Getting this wrong silently inflates the\n    paper's token totals, so the mode is recorded in the run log, not guessed.\n    \"\"\"\n    totals = {key: 0 for key in USAGE_KEYS}\n    last: dict[str, int] | None = None\n    turns = 0\n    for event in events:\n        if event.get(\"type\") != \"turn.completed\":\n            continue\n        usage = event.get(\"usage\")\n        if not isinstance(usage, dict):\n            turn = event.get(\"turn\")\n            usage = turn.get(\"usage\") if isinstance(turn, dict) else None\n        if not isinstance(usage, dict):\n            continue\n        turns += 1\n        normalized = {}\n        for source, target in USAGE_MAP.items():\n            value = usage.get(source)\n            normalized[target] = int(value) if isinstance(value, (int, float)) else 0\n        last = normalized\n        for key, value in normalized.items():\n            totals[key] += value\n    if mode == \"last\" and last is not None:\n
