"d5d6feb4ad8c22da13bf81f320a8056afecb4bf5eee37795451e714480be1b14": {"encoding": "utf8", "content": "# Protocol: issues and pull requests\n\nNormative for the GitHub-backed issue and PR lifecycle and the automation in\n`local/bin/`; read `local/protocols/meta.md` first. The repository is\n`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`, and GitHub is the **single source of truth** for\nissues, PRs, CI and review evidence, and merges; CI and reviews still *execute*\nhere and publish their results there. No active `issues/` or `prs/` tree, no\nshadow record, no write-through cache, no offline mutation mode: a GitHub error\nfails the operation, never a local success (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01).\n\n## 1. Records, names, tools\n\nIssues and PRs are GitHub's, identified by their numbers — no zero-padded ids,\nno frontmatter. Parent/child structure is the native sub-issue relation\n(`POST …/issues/{parent}/sub_issues`), one parent per issue exactly as the\nretired `parent:` scalar allowed; discussion is comments; labels come from the\nrepository (`list-labels`, paginated), so `local/labels.yml` is retired and a\nlabel absent from GitHub is reported, never invented.\n`pr_open.py --issue N` inherits only its explicit descriptive-label allowlist\nfrom issue N, unions it with explicit `--label` values, and adds those labels\nwithout removing existing PR labels. Scheduling, approval and owner-state\nlabels are never inherited. Before push, creation/adoption requires at least\none descriptive label, supplied explicitly, inherited, or already on the PR;\notherwise the command explains how the operator can classify the change.\nGitHub still validates label existence; the allowlist is an inheritance policy,\nnot a replacement registry. Backfills use the same additive API and inspect\nthe actual change when the source issue itself is unlabeled. Briefs (the design record\nper issue) live in `local/briefs/`: agent input, not lifecycle state.\n\nPrerequisites between issues are **GitHub issue dependencies**\n(`GET`/`POST …/issues/{n}/dependencies/blocked_by`), one edge per prerequisite.\nThe edge is retained even when the prerequisite closes, so reopening it restores the block.\nA prerequisite carried by a pull request is the packet issue that PR closes. The\n\"Dependencies\" bullets in an issue body are commentary on those edges, never\nthe record. A packet is **ready** when it is an open leaf of the tracker tree\nand every issue blocking it is closed; `local/bin/ready_packets.py` computes\nthat list, and the operator launches lanes from it rather than from a\nhand-kept order or a dependency table in a comment (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-04).\nEstablish or adopt each edge with\n`local/bin/gh_common.py add-blocked-by ISSUE PREREQUISITE`. The command first\nreads the edge, makes at most one mutation, and re-reads after an ambiguous\nfailure; it is therefore safe to repeat. Record closed prerequisites too.\n\nEvery GitHub call goes through `local/bin/gh_common.py` — a module for Python\ncallers, and for the shell scripts a CLI (`pr-view`, `post-status`,\n`latest-statuses`, `ensure-pr-comment`, `post-review`, `merge-pr`,\n`issue-create`, `add-blocked-by`, `issue-close`, `snapshot`, …; `--help` lists\nthem) owning CLI discovery, repository resolution, API version headers,\nbounded retry of transient failures and the exit-2-with-stderr convention.\nNothing else shells out to `gh`. `issue_new.py`, `issue_close.py`, `pr_open.py`,\n`ci.sh`, `review.sh`, `autofix.sh`, `pr_merge.py`, `github-sync.sh` take GitHub\nnumbers; `track.py`, `validate_tree.py` and `export_issues.py` are deleted.\n\nEvery repository-owned branch publication runs through `checked-push.sh` with\none explicit `refs/heads/...:refs/heads/...` mapping.  The helper reads the\nremote tip with a short `ls-remote`, resolves the local ref's registered\nworktree, and refuses a checkout whose HEAD or working tree differs from the\ncaptured commit.  It runs that checkout's `.githooks/pre-push` against the exact\nref tuple before starting `receive-pack`, then pushes the captured commit under\nan exact remote-tip lease.  The native hook performs a short defense-in-depth\ncomparison when selected, while the helper's lease makes a moved remote ref fail\nclosed even when that hook is stale or absent.  A caller's explicit\n`MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1` remains the documented emergency bypass.  It skips\nvalidation only: implicit tag following stays disabled, so publication remains\nlimited to the explicit branch mapping.\n\n`github-sync.sh [ref ...]` takes branch names (default `main`), not a `push`\nsubcommand. It retains the post-publication record snapshot. When an explicitly\nrequested/default main push succeeded and the snapshot created a new telemetry\ncommit, it checked-pushes main once more without creating another snapshot.\nBranch-only calls never implicitly publish main. Snapshot reads remain best-effort;\nsnapshot commit or final publication failure returns nonzero and leaves the\npreserved local state for the operator to recover.\n\nEvery merge of `github/main` or a stack parent into an issue branch runs the\nmerge-loss guard before the merge commit is created. The guard compares the\npending index with `HEAD`, `MERGE_HEAD`, and every best merge base. It refuses\nan incoming path that disappeared without a branch-side deletion and an\nincoming-only entry restored wholesale to the unchanged branch blob. Paths\nrecorded by Git as conflicts remain resolution decisions. The\n`reference-transaction` hook checks an automatic merge's commit object before\nthe branch ref moves; `pre-commit` checks the pending index for a merge\ncommitted later. Neither path permits `MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS` to bypass this\ncheck. A lane checking an existing merge uses the primary checkout's\n`local/bin/merge_loss_guard.py --repo <worktree> --commit <merge>` so a stale\nbranch copy cannot weaken the audit.\n\n* Branches: `issue-<github-number>-<slug>`, or `codex/issue-<number>-<slug>`\n  from an agent; `pr_open.py` rejects what `git check-ref-format` would.\n* Titles, slugs and branch names are **bracket-free**: bot-generated branch\n  names inherit those characters and \"`]` breaks part of the PR automation\n  stack\" (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124). A `:` in a *title* is fine\n  (`Tracking: …`), but not in a branch.\n* `autofix.sh`'s automated fix commits keep the exact subject prefixes\n  `[codex-auto-fix]` and `[codex-review-fix]`; its iteration counter and the\n  review skip key on them.  Operator and worker repairs use plain\n  `fix(review): …` / `fix(ci): …` subjects so the reviewer sees them.\n* `Closes #N` / `Fixes #N` auto-closes the issue on merge, `Addresses #N` does\n  not (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:61-62) — and the numbers being GitHub's, that\n  footer is now literally what GitHub itself reads.\n\n## 2. Evidence contracts\n\nAll evidence binds to the **exact head SHA** (DESIGN.md invariant 2).\n\n**Commit statuses.** Ten canonical contexts, posted by `post-status`: one\n`local-ci/<step>` per CI step (`build`, `blueprint-render`, `paper-gaps`,\n`blueprint-sync`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`,\n`statement-origin`), plus `local-ci/summary` and `local-review/summary`.\n`ci.sh` posts `pending` before each gate step and `success | failure | error`\nafter it; a gated-out step is a `success` saying it was skipped. The gate reads\nthe *latest* status per context (`latest-statuses`), never GitHub's combined\nstatus, silent as that is about contexts never posted. The run manifest is one\nPR comment marked `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, kept current by\n`ensure-pr-comment`: evidence for humans, while the statuses are the gate.\n\n**Review verdict.** One `COMMENT` review per head SHA, bound to `commit_id`,\ncarrying `<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`, the findings ledger, and the\nline `VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=…, prose=…)`.\nUnchecked findings are ledger lines matching `^\\s*[-*]\\s*\\[ \\]`; clean means\n`APPROVED`, or `COMMENTED` with none of them. Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT`\ntoo — a **single account** cannot approve its own pull request, so the review\nevent carries no authority — and adverseness travels in `local-review/summary`\n(`failure` for unresolved findings), which is the gate's review evidence.\n\n**Adjudication** (review.md §12) is a PR comment whose body starts with\n`ADJUDICATION` and contains `head=<SHA>` for the current head, one disposition\nline per remaining finding; `--adjudicated` takes nothing else.\n\n**Idempotency.** Every publishing step is **at most one mutation**: a paginated\nread finds the stable marker first and adopts that record instead of duplicating\nit (`commentOnce`, issue-automation.yml:403-417, now guarding retries rather than\nwebhook redelivery); an ambiguous write stays pending for adoption.\n\n## 3. The merge gate\n\nSingle-PR merges use `pr_merge.py <number>`; reviewed batches use `pr_train.py`\nas described below. Workers never merge or publish main directly. A single-PR\nmerge is a REST `PUT …/pulls/{n}/merge` with the exact\n`sha` guard, issued by `gh_common.merge_pr` and verified against the merge\ncommit's topology (two parents, the frozen head second), behind seven gates\nthat refuse by default:\n\n1. the PR is open, unmerged and not a draft (`draft is False`, not merely\n   falsy), and reports a head SHA, a head ref and a base ref;\n2. the primary worktree is clean and on the base, and the local branch tip\n   equals the GitHub head SHA — the merge must be of the bytes built here. After\n   fetching the current GitHub base, the head is fresh when that base is its\n   ancestor, or when every raw tree change from their merge base to the base is\n   allowlisted passive telemetry: a regular non-executable (`100644`) `.md` or\n   `.jsonl` file below `results/telemetry/`, or a generated regular\n   non-executable `.json` file below the exact\n   `results/telemetry/github-snapshot/` subtree. The check uses\n   `git diff --raw -z --no-renames` so additions, deletions and both sides of a\n   rename retain their paths and modes. Executable files, executable-mode\n   changes, symlinks, code or unknown suffixes, malformed records, paths outside\n   those boundaries, a missing merge base and every failed Git command block;\n3. all eight `local-ci/<step>` contexts plus `local-ci/summary` are `success` on\n   that exact SHA; a **missing** context blocks, because GitHub's combined state\n   reads `success` for a commit carrying no statuses at all;\n4. that SHA's marker-bound `COMMENT` review (or one carried forward per\n   review.md §13) carries `VERDICT: APPROVED`, or\n   `COMMENTED` with zero unchecked findings, **and** `local-review/summary` is\n   `success` there;\n5. no `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review stands on that head, from anyone;\n6. no live fix lock for the branch (`locks/fix-<branch>.lock`, running holder);\n   the count of `merge-base..head` commits whose subject starts with a §1 fix\n   prefix is printed for the record and is not a gate;\n7. every issue the PR body closes — all nine of GitHub's closing keywords, not\n   just `Closes` — has no open sub-issue left.\n\n`--adjudicated` waives gate 4's adverse verdict and nothing else, and only when\nan exact-head `ADJUDICATION` comment backs it; gate 5 is never adjudicable.\n\n**Merge subject.** Past the gates, the merge is given the subject\n`Merge PR #N: <PR title> [lean +A -D]`, where A and D sum the added and deleted\nlines of `git diff --numstat <merge base>...<head> -- '*.lean'` and a PR that\nchanges no Lean line reads `[lean 0]`; the title is sanitized, collapsed to one\nline and truncated to 80 characters, and the one-line body names the frozen head\nSHA. They travel as the REST `commit_title` / `commit_message` merge keys, which\n`gh_common.merge_pr` omits entirely when its optional arguments are absent. The\ncount is an **approximate** size signal for GitHub's commits page (issue #557),\nnever evidence: it is measured after every gate, nothing reads it back, and a\nfailed measurement sends no wording at all — GitHub then titles the merge as it\nalways did, and the merge still happens. Closing keywords in the title are\ndefused first (`closes #900` reads `closes issue 900` in the subject): gate 7\nchecked the PR body and the branch commits, never the subject, so a merge commit\nmust not be able to close an issue whose open sub-issues nobody examined.\n`pr_merge.py --check-only` prints the subject it would use, so the operator can\nread it before the merge.\n\nAfterwards a best-effort, non-fatal tail fast-forwards local `main` to the\nremote merge commit; branch and worktree cleanup keeps its safeguards (local\ndirt defers it with a warning).\n\n### Reviewed merge trains\n\nAfter independent review and deployment, the daemon/operator may invoke\n`local/bin/pr_train.py N M [K ...]` from the clean primary checkout at\n`github/main`. Development and tests use fixture repositories exclusively.\nEvery member passes the existing open, local-tip, exact-head CI, independent\nreview, changes-requested, fix-lock, and dependency gates. Repeat\n`--adjudicated N` only for members with the existing exact-head adjudication\nrecord. A precondition failure refuses the entire batch and names the member.\nThe individual-head base-ancestry requirement is replaced by mandatory CI of\nthe combined commit; member review evidence is neither copied nor rewritten.\n\nThe tool creates `train-<UTC-stamp>` and a private worktree under the runtime\ncache, merging frozen member SHAs with two-parent merge commits in argument\norder. A conflict aborts only that merge, verifies restoration of the accepted\ntrain, and drops that member; fewer than two accepted members refuses the batch.\nThe primary merge-loss guard checks each accepted merge. Existing developer\nbranches and worktrees are preserved. Failed train worktrees remain for diagnosis.\n\n`ci.sh --integration-head SHA --worktree PATH --base SHA` runs all eight steps\nagainst the combined commit, using one locked build of the complete `MIPStarRE`\nlibrary and `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`. This includes the root artifact\nneeded by publication's dynamic `checkdecls` import and all downstream modules.\nIt rejects skip flags and dirty or moved train\nheads, and publishes no PR evidence. Its manifest and logs stay in the runtime\ncache. Bootstrap and build telemetry are transferred to the primary telemetry\nfiles after publication, refusal, or an unknown outcome so their appends cannot dirty the primary\nduring gating; the transfer and the train event use the canonical\n`telemetry.py` writers, so they obey the locking every other session obeys. CI warming uses `--no-build` to avoid a nested build lock, and\nstep execution stops at its first failing command.\n\nPublication uses `checked-push.sh --train-manifest PATH` with one explicit\ntrain-to-main ref mapping. After preflight, it rechecks the combined CI manifest,\nmember gates and heads, primary cleanliness, and frozen main; the existing exact\nremote-tip lease protects the final fast-forward. Because a recheck only reads\nthe member refs, the same atomic transport leases every verified member ref at\nits verified value: an untouched member is already up to date and stays out of\nthe transaction, while a member that moved makes the remote reject the whole\npush, main included, and no member branch is ever rewound. Hook bypass is\nforbidden.\nGitHub recognizes included PRs by ancestry; the tool closes no issue by hand.\nIt posts one idempotent train comment per member, records one merge event,\nfast-forwards local main and its origin alias, and removes only the train branch\nand worktree. A failure after publication is reported as such and requires\noperator reconciliation; it must not be retried as a new merge. An ambiguous\npush is reconciled against remote main: equality or verified ancestry containing\nthe train establishes publication. Failed reads, unavailable ancestry, and\nnegative ancestry in a shallow repository retain an explicit `unknown` outcome.\nAn unknown outcome is never a refusal or permission to retry. The runtime\n`publication.json`, stderr, and telemetry retain that distinction; unresolved\nworktrees and manifests remain available for operator reconciliation. Generated\nbranch names are single components accepted by external Lake-root bootstrap.\nDeployment and\ndaemon wiring remain separate from development of this tool (issue #502).\n\n### Main-cycle integration checkpoint\n\nThe active owner service records, at each bounded tick, the local `main` SHA,\nthe readable remote `refs/heads/main` SHA, primary cleanliness, transport\nresult, and the age and exact head of the oldest CI-and-review-eligible open\nPR. A dirty primary, remote mismatch, unavailable transport, active fix or\ntransaction lock, missing configured Space allocation or external-zero gate, or a stale\ncandidate is\na HOLD reason; it is never silently converted into a merge attempt. After a\nsuccessful daemon-owned merge, the service re-reads remote `main` and records\nthe new SHA before the next tick. The service may invoke `pr_merge.py` only as\nits daemon-owned final action after these checks; workers never merge directly.\nEach tick has bounded Git/GitHub reads and records failures as HOLD rather than\nexiting the loop. The cadence is monotonic: work time is subtracted from the\nconfigured interval (default 300 seconds). Candidate records distinguish stale\nexact-head PRs from fresh actionable PRs using `pr_merge.head_is_fresh`, the\nsame conservative predicate as gate 2b; `pr_age_s` is PR creation age, while\neligibility onset remains unknown unless separately observed.\n\n## 4. Untrusted text\n\nIssue and PR bodies are untrusted data, and **more** so now that they arrive\nfrom GitHub: anyone with repository access, and every imported external report,\nwrites the fields that are echoed into generated markdown and interpolated into\nagent prompts. All three parent workflows sanitized before interpolation, and\n`wf_util.sanitize` is that step ported: strip control characters, break fenced\ncode with zero-width spaces, truncate to 200 characters for titles and 5000 for\nbodies (issue-automation.yml:122-128).\n\nEvery LLM hook in `local/bin` carries the same four requirements: gate on\n`MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED != \"false\"`; read prompts from committed main\n(`git show main:…`), never the branch under review (DESIGN.md:76-77); frame\nsanitized text as data that must not be followed; and filter any model-proposed\nlabel through the repository's label list. `audit_stale_issues.py` additionally\nkeeps its path-traversal rejection for externally sourced citations.\n\n## 5. Environment, snapshot, archive\n\n`MIPSTARRE_GH` is the path to `gh` (else `PATH`, else the documented user-local\nlocation); `MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO` overrides the `owner/name` otherwise read\nfrom the `github` remote; `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP` (default 5) bounds `autofix.sh`'s\nown loop only — the merge gate does not read it — and is operator-tunable with\nthe reason recorded in `results/telemetry/events.md`, unlike\n`MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE` (the pre-commit budget), the one owner-gated control\nin the layer. `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` and\n`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` keep kill-switch semantics (DESIGN.md:73-75).\n\n`github-sync.sh` pushes explicit refs and writes an atomic, paginated read-only\nsnapshot of open issues and PRs to `results/telemetry/github-snapshot/`\n(and, since the push goes through `checked-push.sh`, commits that snapshot and\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` to the primary checkout so the next publish\nfinds a clean tree)\n(`open-issues.json`, `open-pulls.json`, `metadata.json`; PRs filtered out of the\nissue endpoint) — audit and recovery telemetry, never lifecycle input. The\nretired trees stay archived under `results/telemetry/registry-archive/` (commit\nc8f1999): read-only research data, never edited or read as active input.\n\n## 6. Owner inbox and mathematical-gap escalation\n\nPinned issue #26 is the owner inbox: it receives only decisions that require\nthe human owner. A source statement found to be mathematically false does not\ngo there first. Following the availability report on #26 and the September 6\nowner decision, main selects Astra Ultra for the mathematical-gap lane through\n`MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-6-astra local/bin/dispatch.sh --role mathfix --effort ultra`.\nHistorical owner-launched Fable measurements remain unchanged. Every request or\ndispatch carries the exact source path, label and line range; the counterexample\nor obstruction; the paper-gap note; the relevant blueprint dependency graph and\nLean consumers; and the cumulative session count and elapsed working time.\n\nA correction is adopted only when it meets all four conditions below.\n\n1. **Correctness:** the known counterexample no longer applies, adversarial\n   checks find no replacement counterexample, and a mathematical proof sketch\n   derives the corrected conclusion from its explicit hypotheses using cited\n   source results.\n2. **Sufficiency:** every use in the paper and every dependent node in the\n   blueprint graph remains justified; checking only the first Lean consumer is\n   insufficient.\n3. **Minimality:** the correction is the closest sufficient statement to the\n   source, with no unnecessary hypothesis or weakened conclusion and no change\n   to the source semantics; definition or game corrections require an explicit\n   faithfulness audit and independent mathematical review.\n4. **Lean convergence:** the corrected statement type-checks and all affected\n   downstream consumers compile. Lean success alone does not establish the\n   preceding three conditions.\n\nThe operator iterates mathematics and Lean for at most ten `mathfix` sessions\nor about one and a half working days per gap, whichever comes first. The budget\nis shared across the historical owner-launched Fable lane and the Astra lane; a\nmodel or telemetry change does not reset it. Main decides mathematical\ncorrections with the preceding evidence and independent review, including\ndefinition/game corrections that preserve the intended source semantics;\nchanging the project goal is outside that authority. If the current authorized\nbudget expires, stop that lane and record the attempted statements,\ncounterexamples, proof sketches and unresolved consumers on #27 and in the gap\nnote. Do not reset attempts or working time. Use #26 only for an owner-only\npermission, credential, access or scope/resource grant; mathematical difficulty\nalone is not an owner decision. An already-posted #26 item waits for the owner\nunless the owner explicitly returns it to main.\n\nAn adopted correction follows the ordinary CI and independent-review gates. Do not accept a conditional\n   helper as the default repair path.\n   Existing conditional helpers must have names that make the conditional nature clear,\n   cite the unresolved source obligation, state a removal plan, and must not be treated as\n   the paper theorem or advertised by `\\leanok`.\n   A newly introduced conditional helper, proof-debt bundle, producer, witness, wrapper, or obligation\n   package is itself a blocker unless the PR is explicitly a paper-realignment change,\n   the new object preserves useful proof content from an already drifting statement, and\n   the paper-facing theorem remains source-faithful.\n4. 🟡 **Mathlib style**: Does the code follow Mathlib conventions? State the theorem, lemma, definition, or proof obligation directly.\n\n**Reading existing feedback:**\nBefore posting new comments, read ALL existing feedback on this PR using the GitHub MCP tools:\n1. Read **inline review threads** via `get_review_comments` — these are code-level comments from previous review cycles.\n2. Read **PR conversation comments** via `get_comments` — bots and humans often post feedback, summaries,\n   and discussion directly on the PR thread (not as inline review comments). Only resolve bot threads — never resolve threads authored by human reviewers.\n   This prevents stale bot comments from accumulating across review cycles.\n\n**Example: How to fetch thread IDs and resolve them**\n\nStep 1 — Query thread IDs via GraphQL (returns up to 100 threads; see Step 3 for pagination):\n```bash\ngh api graphql -f query='\n{\n  repository(owner: \"<REPOSITORY_OWNER>\", name: \"<REPOSITORY_NAME>\") {\n    pullRequest(number: <PR_NUMBER>) {\n      reviewThreads(first: 100) {\n        nodes {\n          id\n          isResolved\n          isOutdated\n          comments(first: 1) {\n            nodes {\n              author { login }\n              body\n            }\n          }\n        }\n        pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}'\n```\nThis returns thread objects with `id` fields like `\"PRRT_kwDON...\"`. Use pagination if `hasNextPage` is true.\n\nStep 2 — For each unresolved bot thread whose issue is now fixed, resolve it:\n```\nmcp__github__resolve_review_thread(threadId: \"PRRT_kwDON...\")\n```\n\nStep 3 — If there are more than 100 threads, paginate:\n```bash\ngh api graphql -f query='\n{\n  repository(owner: \"<REPOSITORY_OWNER>\", name: \"<REPOSITORY_NAME>\") {\n    pullRequest(number: <PR_NUMBER>) {\n      reviewThreads(first: 100, after: \"CURSOR_FROM_PREVIOUS_PAGE\") {\n        nodes { id isResolved isOutdated comments(first: 1) { nodes { author { login } body } } }\n        pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}'\n```\n"}, "3b14bf8ec263e46bafe6648203ec6f624e47f217c907bc0d2064ca24c2e99f60": {"encoding": "utf8", "content": "This is a Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization project for quantum complexity theory\n(MIP* = RE and low-degree tests). This is the **single\nsource of truth** for agent conventions. Claude Code agents should also read\n`CLAUDE.md` for Claude-specific notes.\n\n## Project Overview\n\nThis repository is a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization project for mathematics\naround $MIP^* = RE$. It is the **local-only continuation** of\n[LionSR/MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE): the inherited track is\nthe **low individual degree test (LDT)** paper (arXiv:2009.12982); the active\ntrack is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from *MIP\\*=RE*\n(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and *NEEXP in MIP\\** (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).\n\nCI, review, and auto-fix **execute locally**; issues, PRs, their evidence and\nmerges live on GitHub (`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`), reached only through\n`local/bin/gh_common.py`. Read `local/README.md` and `local/DESIGN.md` before\ndoing workflow actions; the `## Local Operations` section below summarizes the\nrules.\n\nKey locations:\n\n- `references/qpbt-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of MIP\\*=RE\n  (arXiv:2001.04383); the QPBT lives in\n  `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex` and\n  `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex`\n- `references/neexp-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of NEEXP in MIP\\*\n  (arXiv:1904.05870); secondary source\n  (`07_a_self_test_for_the_pauli_basis.tex`)\n- `references/ldt-paper/` — in-repo TeX source mirror for LDT\n- `blueprint/src/` — active LaTeX blueprint with Lean cross-references\n  (`\\lean{}`, `\\leanok`)\n- `MIPStarRE/` — Lean codebase matching the blueprint\n- `audits/` — dated audit reports, scouting notes, and repair plans\n- `local/`, `results/telemetry/` — the local workflow layer\n\nA legacy 2111 tensor track exists under `blueprint/legacy/` — do not modify it.\n\n**Canonical source hierarchy** (use in this order):\n\n1. `references/` paper mirrors — TeX source of the papers\n2. `blueprint/src/chapter/` — active LaTeX blueprint\n3. `MIPStarRE/` — Lean scaffold\n\nAlways read the paper source before formalizing or proving a statement. The\npaper contains the precise mathematical definitions, theorem statements, and\nproof strategies that the Lean code must faithfully represent. When stuck on a\nsorry site or proof, go back to the original paper TeX source — the answer is\nalmost always there. Do not guess or try random tactics without first\nunderstanding the paper's proof strategy.\n\n## Repository Layout\n\n```\nMIPStarRE/\n├── Quantum/               # Reusable matrix / measurement infrastructure\n│   ├── FiniteMatrix.lean  # Op d, normalizedTrace, tauNormSq, IsProj, ...\n│   └── Measurement.lean   # POVM, measurement types\n└── LDT/                   # Low individual degree test (13 submodules)\n    ├── Basic/             # Parameters, operators, distributions, submeasurements\n    ├── Test/              # Test definitions & main theorem\n    ├── Preliminaries/\n    ├── MakingMeasurementsProjective/\n    ├── MainInductionStep/\n    ├── ExpansionHypercubeGraph/\n    ├── GlobalVariance/\n    ├── SelfImprovement/\n    ├── CommutativityPoints/\n    ├── Commutativity/\n    └── Pasting/\n```\n\nEach LDT submodule typically has `Defs.lean` and `Theorems.lean`. Root imports\nflow: `MIPStarRE.lean` → `Quantum` + `LDT` → all submodules.\n\n## Quick Start — Build and Check Commands\n\nRun commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.\n\n### First-time setup\n\n```bash\nlake exe cache get\nlake build\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check\n```\n\nRun the hook check in every fresh worktree before preparing a PR.  The hooks\nmove fast statement-integrity, proof-debt, changed-file Lean, and blueprint-sync\nchecks to the local workflow so CI is not spent on preventable statement drift.\n\n### Full project build (CI-equivalent)\n\n```bash\nlake build\n```\n\n### Fast single-file type-check (default iteration loop)\n\n```bash\nlake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in one file\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean || true\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in the whole project\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE\n```\n\n### Declaration checker\n\n```bash\nlake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls\n```\n\nUse this when blueprint declaration lists need to match Lean declarations.\n\n### Blueprint build\n\n```bash\nleanblueprint pdf    # PDF output\nleanblueprint web    # HTML output (use as default for quick checks)\n```\n\nIn CI, blueprint linting effectively runs `leanblueprint web` from `blueprint/`.\n\n### What counts as a single test\n\nThis repository does not have a conventional unit-test suite. The closest\nsingle-test commands are:\n\n- **Lean work**: `lake env lean path/to/File.lean` and\n  `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\" path/to/File.lean || true`\n- **Blueprint work**: `leanblueprint web`\n- **Whole-repo verification**: `lake build` and\n  `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n### Recommended validation sequence\n\nFor a Lean file change:\n\n1. Type-check the edited file with `lake env lean ...`\n2. Scan that file for `sorry|axiom`\n3. If the change affects imports or shared declarations, run `lake build`\n\nFor blueprint changes:\n\n1. Run `leanblueprint web`\n2. If declaration links changed, run `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n## Toolchain\n\n- **Lean**: v4.31.0 (from `lean-toolchain`)\n- **Mathlib**: v4.31.0 (from `lakefile.toml`)\n\nImportant `lakefile.toml` options:\n\n- `relaxedAutoImplicit = false` — declare all variables explicitly\n- `pp.unicode.fun = true`\n- `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true`\n- `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`\n\n## Proof-Filling Order\n\nSections must be filled in this dependency order:\n\n1. Sections 3–4: test setup and preliminaries\n2. Section 5: making measurements projective\n3. Sections 7–8: expansion and global variance\n4. Section 9: self-improvement\n5. Sections 10–11: commutativity\n6. Section 12: pasting\n7. Section 6: main induction wrapper\n\nDo not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.\n\n## Faithful Formalization Policy\n\nA declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean\nstatement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in\n`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a\nfaithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.\nThis applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper\nresult, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the\nhypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose\nconclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra\nload-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not\nthe paper theorem.\nThe project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize\nthem as permanent infrastructure.\n\nIf the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must\nnot mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either\nleave the source-labelled entry without `\\leanok`, or state the restricted or\nconditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are\ndisplayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\\leanok` only\nagainst a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must\nnot be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.\n\nWhen a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a\nsource theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.\nThe note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of\nthe cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,\nderiving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.\n\nThis rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as\n`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked\nfrom the blueprint by `\\lean{...}` and `\\leanok`.\n\nBefore editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,\n`prop:*`):\n\n1. Read the corresponding statement in `references/ldt-paper/`.\n2. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are\n   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.\n3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer\n   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary\n   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.\n4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named\n   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.\n5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A\n   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it\n   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains\n   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem\n   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its\n   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like\n   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example\n   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a\n   name ending in `_ofObligations`.\n6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper\n   with `\\leanok`.\n\nWhen reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package\nhypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction\nand turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not\nactually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as\na strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave\nthe missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a\ntracked `sorry` during a repair PR.\n\nSome side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a\ndivision, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model\ninstances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of\nassumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is\ndifferent: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such\nas a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,\n`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the\npaper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\n\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\n`\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions.  A theorem\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\n\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\nintegrity audit:\n\n- paper assumptions;\n- Lean assumptions;\n- paper conclusion;\n- Lean conclusion;\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\n\n### Paper-realignment mode\n\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\n\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\n\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\n\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\n\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\n\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\nhypotheses.\n\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\nminimal form is:\n\n```text\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\n```\n\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\ndeviation has been discharged.\n\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker.  If the paper\nhas a local typo, a documented numerical strengthening, or a genuine scope\nrestriction, use a lighter docstring marker such as `**Local fix:**` or\n`**Scope restriction:**`, citing the relevant paper-gap note.  These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\n  tactic blocks.\n\n### Naming conventions\n\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\n\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\n\nProject-preferred variable names:\n\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\n- `σ` — strategies\n- `P` — projective measurements\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\n\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\n\n### Types and signatures\n\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\n  wrappers\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\n\n### Documentation\n\nRequired:\n\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\n- Cite blueprint nodes by their stable LaTeX label, for example blueprint\n  `lem:cl-concat`. Do not store blueprint line numbers in Lean docstrings. When\n  reviewing, derive the current span with\n  `python3 scripts/blueprint_citations.py resolve lem:cl-concat`.\n- Cite paper mirrors by a paper label when one exists, or by a repository path\n  plus a narrow anchored passage when the source has no suitable label. Paper\n  mirror line ranges are acceptable because those mirrors are immutable.\n\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\lean{...}`\nand `\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\n\n## Proof Engineering\n\n### Search before proving\n\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\n\n### Mathlib integration\n\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\n\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\n\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n### Validation ladder\n\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\n2. `lake build`\n\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\n\n### Lean-specific advice\n\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\n  already in the repo\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\n\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\n\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\nmathematical phrase is available.\n\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\npaper, and the local formalization. Do not invent slang or private shorthand for\nmathematical objects. The goal is prose that a third-party reader can understand\nwithout having read the agent conversation that produced the change.\n\n### Paper-gap notes\n\nFor the proof-gap terminology used to distinguish source theorems, internal\nproof obligations, and conditional helpers, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.  For documentation of discrepancies\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If Lean uses a Mathlib result or\nconstruction not present in the cited argument, explain that replacement\npedagogically before naming the formal declaration. If the cited assertion is\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\n\n## Proof Integrity\n\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\n\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\n\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\n\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\n\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\n\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\n\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\n\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. Ask: *Can a real proof be built on top\nof this?*\n\n### Warnings\n\nPlaceholder tactics (`exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`) should be replaced\nwith concrete results. Debug artifacts (`dbg_trace`, `#check`, `#eval`,\n`#print`) should be removed from proof files. See the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference for\nthe full warning catalog.\n\n### Anti-patterns\n\nSubtler proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks yet still fail to\nprove the claimed mathematics are catalogued in `docs/anti_patterns.md`:\nconclusion-shaped hypotheses, definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback\nbranches, trivial default witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, and external\n`*Statement` smuggles. Reviewers should consult this file alongside\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md`.\n\n## PR and Commit Conventions\n\nPRs are GitHub pull requests (opened by `local/bin/pr_open.py`, merged by\n`local/bin/pr_merge.py`); `#N` in PR bodies and commit messages is the GitHub\nissue number. Titles, bodies, and commit rules below are unchanged from the\nparent project.\n\n### PR title format\n\n```\ntype(scope): short description\n```\n\n| Type       | When to use                                      |\n|------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |\n| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |\n| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |\n| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |\n| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |\n| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |\n| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |\n\n**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`,\n`blueprint`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.\n\n### PR body template\n\nEvery PR body must contain three sections:\n\n```markdown\n### Motivation\n- Why this change is needed. Cite the issue and paper/blueprint location.\n\n### Description\n- State precisely what changed.\n\n### Testing\n- What was verified and how (e.g., `lake build`, `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\"`).\n\n---\nAddresses #N\n```\n\nUse `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge).\n\n### Commit messages\n\n- **Imperative mood** in the subject line (\"Add\", not \"Added\")\n- Subject under 72 characters\n- When squash-merging, the commit message should match the PR title format\n\n## Review Process\n\nEvery PR touching Lean code is reviewed by a dedicated local reviewer session\n(`local/bin/review.sh`, dispatched after green local CI; a session never\nreviews its own diff) against these criteria:\n\n1. **Proof correctness** — No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.\n2. **Mathlib style** — Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_doc` references.\n3. **Paper terminology** — Public Lean names and documentation should use\n   terminology from the paper and blueprint. See `docs/mathematical_language.md`.\n4. **Linter hygiene** — Fix warnings, don't mask them with broad\n   `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks.\n5. **Type safety** — No universe mismatches, coercion problems.\n6. **Performance** — Avoid expensive tactics on large types.\n7. **Modularity** — Are new lemmas general enough to be reused?\n8. **Documentation** — Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.\n9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** — Add `\\lean{}` and `\\leanok` tags for\n   formalized statements only when the Lean statement matches the source.\n   Record formalization-only auxiliary lemmas explicitly.\n10. **Scaffolding integrity** — Verify scaffolding aligns with Mathlib.\n11. **Statement drift** — Compare source-labelled theorem statements with the\n   paper and flag new hypotheses, weakened conclusions, changed quantifier\n   order, altered error parameters, or bridge/residual packages moving toward\n   a paper theorem.\n12. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** — Review against `docs/anti_patterns.md`.\n\nFor full details, see `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` and the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review` reference.\n\n## Blueprint and Documentation Work\n\nIf modifying blueprint material:\n\n- Keep chapter structure under `blueprint/src/chapter/`\n- Ensure `leanblueprint web` succeeds\n- Keep Lean declaration references valid\n- Sync theorem labels with Lean names\n- Add `\\lean{LeanDeclName}` and `\\leanok` tags for formalized statements\n\nFor blueprint style conventions, see `docs/blueprint_style_guide.md`.\n\nFor temporary conditional scaffolding and the `\\lean{}`/`\\leanok` tagging\nstrategy, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n## Agent Rule Sources\n\nChecked in this repository snapshot:\n\n- No `.cursorrules`\n- No `.cursor/rules/`\n- No `.github/copilot-instructions.md`\n\n### Skills\n\nThe `texra-lean-skills` plugin (texra-ai/texra-lean-skills) carries the\ncanonical Mathlib-style, proof-integrity, and prose convention texts as the\n`lean-conventions` skill. Claude Code installs it automatically via\n`.claude/settings.json`; other agents install it by cloning the\nrepository and symlinking the skill directories into their skill\nlocation, as described in its README.\nMIPStarRE-local addenda to those conventions live in\n`docs/project_conventions.md`, which restates no shared rule.\n\nUse this file together with:\n\n| File | Purpose |\n|------|---------|\n| `CLAUDE.md` | Claude Code-specific notes (minimal pointer to this file) |\n| `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` | PR format, issue templates, label taxonomy, review checklist |\n| `lean-conventions` skill | Mathlib style, naming, documentation, PR review, proof integrity, prose style (canonical; installed) |\n| `docs/project_conventions.md` | MIPStarRE-local addenda to the shared conventions |\n| `docs/anti_patterns.md` | Subtler proof-evasion patterns |\n| `docs/proof_frontier_review.md` | Review checklist for construction theorems and residual inputs |\n| `docs/mathematical_language.md` | Project-local terminology rules |\n| `docs/blueprint_style_guide.md` | Blueprint notation and section conventions |\n| `docs/api_surface.md` | Useful obligation-closing lemmas for `SubMeas` |\n| `docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex` | Paper-gap documentation conventions |\n| `docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex` | Protocol distinguishing source theorems, proof obligations, and conditional helpers |\n| `docs/formalization-patterns.md` | Conditional scaffolding, blueprint sync, split imports, and bridge records |\n| `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md` | Pedagogical notes on Mathlib and external lemmas |\n| `docs/ci-automation.md` | GitHub-era CI/CD reference (inactive; see `local/`) |\n| `docs/pr_review_management.md` | GitHub-era review-bot reference (lessons still apply; mechanism replaced by `local/protocols/review.md`) |\n| `local/DESIGN.md` | Local operations architecture and invariants |\n| `local/protocols/` | Normative protocols (meta, build cache, CI, review, auto-fix, issues/PRs, sessions) |\n| `local/personas/` | System prompts for locally dispatched agent roles |\n| `audits/` | Chapter-by-chapter scouting reports |\n| Pinned memories (external agent tooling) | Agent session memory maintained by the agent runtime; not a directory in the repository checkout. Pinned memories contain accumulated project lessons |\n\n## Local Operations\n\nThis repository runs its whole workflow locally. The short version every\nagent must know:\n\n- **Build reuse.** A hot main cache lives under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/`;\n  fresh worktrees get it via `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` (which also\n  installs git hooks and resets dirty vendored packages). Never run\n  `lake update`; never write to the cache; at most one full `lake build`\n  runs machine-wide (the scripts take the lock for you).\n- **Lifecycle.** GitHub issue → branch `issue-<number>-slug` + worktree →\n  agent sessions → `local/bin/ci.sh` → `local/bin/review.sh` → optional\n  `local/bin/autofix.sh` → `local/bin/pr_merge.py`. CI and review evidence are\n  exact-head commit statuses (`local-ci/*`, `local-review/summary`); merges go\n  through GitHub with an exact-SHA guard. Details: `local/README.md`,\n  `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`.\n- **Sessions.** Worker Codex sessions use `local/bin/dispatch.sh` (roles: orc,\n  prover, reviewer, simplifier, blueprint, splitter, scout; `mathfix` is\n  reserved for astra after the #26 availability report) so token/time telemetry\n  stays complete. Lease-backed native descendants are retired by issue #505;\n  `local/protocols/sessions.md` retains their history. Current Fable 5.1\n  math-fix sessions are owner-launched and use `owner-sessions.jsonl`.\n- **Telemetry duty.** Incidents go to `results/telemetry/events.md`;\n  protocol changes follow `local/protocols/meta.md` and are ledgered in\n  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.\n- **Fix commits**: `autofix.sh`'s automated commits are prefixed\n  `[codex-auto-fix]` / `[codex-review-fix]` exactly (the review skip keys on\n  them); operator and worker repairs use plain `fix(review): …` /\n  `fix(ci): …` subjects so they are reviewed. Issue titles, slugs, and branch\n  names stay bracket-free.\n\n## Practical Defaults for Agents\n\nWhen editing Lean code:\n\n1. Read the paper source\n2. Read the target Lean file and nearby supporting files\n3. Type-check the single file\n4. Scan for `sorry|axiom`\n5. Run `lake build` only when the local change is stable\n\nWhen editing blueprint files:\n\n1. Read the matching paper source and chapter file\n2. Update Lean links carefully\n3. Run `leanblueprint web`\n\nPrefer minimal, dependency-aware changes that preserve the project's theorem\nstructure.\n"}, "1ba7d7009e977a7248f830feb99d8a0869db26286e9814d2176769f6848158f5": {"encoding": "utf8", "content": "# Contributing to MIPStarRE\n\nThis document codifies the conventions for pull requests, issues, code review,\nLean style, and CI automation used in the MIPStarRE project.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Pull Request Conventions\n\n### Title format\n\nUse **conventional-commit** style:\n\n```\ntype(scope): short description\n```\n\n| Type       | When to use                                      |\n|------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |\n| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |\n| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |\n| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |\n| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |\n| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |\n| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |\n\n**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`, `blueprint`,\n`LDT/Pasting`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.\n\nExamples:\n- `feat(LDT/SelfImprovement): add self-improvement induction step`\n- `fix(blueprint): resolve broken labels in chapter 7`\n- `refactor(LDT): extract shared preliminaries into Basic module`\n\n### Body template\n\nEvery PR body must contain three sections. For mathematical changes, the body\nshould be readable by someone who has not seen the associated conversation:\ncite the paper or blueprint location, give the theorem label when one exists,\nand state the mathematical assertion precisely.\n\n```markdown\n### Motivation\n- Why this mathematical or documentation change is needed.\n- Cite the issue and, when applicable, the paper/blueprint file, line, and label.\n\n### Description\n- State precisely what changed: definitions introduced, lemmas/theorems proved,\n  blueprint labels updated, and any deliberate difference from the paper statement.\n\n### Testing\n- What was verified and how.\n- Examples: `lake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic.lean`, `lake build MIPStarRE`,\n  `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic.lean || true`.\n\n---\nAddresses #N\n```\n\nUse `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge)\nin the footer to link the relevant issue.\n\n### PR template\n\nA PR template (`.github/pull_request_template.md`) auto-fills the\nMotivation / Description / Testing sections. Fill in the placeholders — do not\ndelete the headings.\n\n### Local hooks\n\nThe repository includes opt-in Git hooks for catching fast statement-integrity\nand blueprint-sync failures before they reach CI:\n\n```bash\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hook runs whitespace, the `scripts/tests` unit tests when any\n`scripts/**/*.py` or `scripts/tests/**` file is staged, the blueprint LaTeX\nconvention lint (`check_blueprint_latex.py`) when blueprint sources or the\nlint helper are staged, and the\npaper-gap-note structure and proof-debt audits on relevant staged files,\nincluding agent prompts and actions under `.github/`.  The pre-push hook\nchecks changed Lean files with `lake env lean`, repeats the fast\nstatement-integrity audits for relevant policy or prompt surfaces, and checks\nblueprint declaration synchronization when Lean or blueprint surfaces changed.\nRepository tools publish through `local/bin/checked-push.sh`, which runs that\ngate before opening the long-lived push transport; `pr_open.py`,\n`github-sync.sh`, and `autofix.sh` use it automatically.  For a direct branch\npublication, pass one full branch mapping to the helper instead of invoking\n`git push` directly.\nThese hooks also reject explicit `axiom` and `constant` declarations in the LDT\ntree; use a tracked `sorry` for an unfinished source-faithful proof instead of\nturning the missing proof into a new ambient assumption.\nFor larger PRs, set `MIPSTARRE_HOOK_FULL=1` when invoking the checked-push helper.\nUse `MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1` only for a one-off local-tooling bypass (the\nworkflow-layer line budget of `.githooks/pre-commit` still runs), and still\nreport the corresponding validation in the PR body.  The bypass skips checks,\nnot the helper's explicit one-ref publication boundary.\n\n### Labels\n\nApply all relevant labels from the taxonomy in [Section 4](#4-label-taxonomy).\n\n---\n\n## 2. Issue Conventions\n\n### Issue templates\n\nThree issue templates are available in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`:\n\n| Template | When to use |\n|----------|-------------|\n| **Formalization Issue** | A specific theorem, definition, construction, or lemma to formalize |\n| **Bug Report** | Broken proof, type error, sorry regression, statement mismatch, or CI failure |\n| **Tracking Issue** | Umbrella issue for a chapter, theorem family, or proof stage, using GitHub sub-issues |\n\n### Formalization issues\n\nUse a descriptive, **bracket-free** title that names the mathematical content:\n\n```\nChapter 9 — finish the sandwich-chain corollaries in ComparisonLemmas\n```\n\nAvoid prefixes like `[Chapter 9] ...`: bot-generated branch names inherit those\ncharacters, and `]` breaks part of the PR automation stack. See\n[`pr_review_management.md`](pr_review_management.md) for the rationale.\n\nFor formalization issues, usually start with `formalization` + `2009.12982`,\nthen add the most specific live chapter or theorem-family labels that apply (for\nexample `ldt-basic`, `preliminaries`, `commutativity`, `pasting`,\n`main-induction`, `proof`, `proof-infra`, `statement-fix`,\n`sorry-elimination`, `mismatch`, `follow-up`, `blueprint`, or\n`blueprint-sync`). Documentation-only or tooling issues should use\n`documentation`, `ci`, `cleanup`, and/or `refactor` instead of\n`formalization`.\n\nWhen the work concerns content that exists only in the blueprint and not in\nthe original paper (arXiv:2009.12982), apply the `blueprint-only` label\nalongside the chapter or theorem-family labels.  Omit `blueprint-only` when the\nwork concerns a statement or definition that appears in the paper.  An issue\nmay need both `2009.12982` and `blueprint-only` when it spans paper-present\ncontent and blueprint-exclusive scaffolding or auxiliary lemmas; in that case\napply both labels so the scope is explicit.\n\nEvery formalization issue must give enough mathematical source information to\nmake the issue self-contained:\n\n- Paper source: a path under `references/ldt-paper/`, line number, theorem or\n  equation label when available, and a short quotation or precise paraphrase.\n- Blueprint source: a path under `blueprint/src/chapter/`, line number, label,\n  and the matching `\\lean{...}` status when relevant.\n- Lean target: the expected declaration name and file path, if already known.\n- Dependencies: theorem labels, existing Lean declarations, and GitHub\n  sub-issues that must precede the statement.\n\nFor issues or PRs touching a source-labelled theorem, include a statement\nintegrity check.  List the paper assumptions, the Lean assumptions, the paper\nconclusion, the Lean conclusion, and a verdict: exact, faithful boundary\nhypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is\nstrongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a\ndocumented mathematical necessity.\nFaithful boundary hypotheses include formal domain data such as nonemptiness,\ndecidability, field-model instances, positivity of parameters, or denominator\nnonvanishing when these are implicit in the source.  Extra bridge, residual,\nrepair, or obligation-structure assumptions are not boundary hypotheses; they\nmake the Lean result conditional.  Do not attach them to a paper-facing theorem.\nIf they are unavoidable while preserving downstream proof work, quarantine them\nin a separately named conditional helper, cite the paper-gap note or tracking\nissue, name the obligation discharger that must remove them, and keep the source\ntheorem statement visible even if its proof contains a tracked `sorry`.\nFor the terminology used here, see the proof-gap protocol in\n[paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex).\n\nDo not describe a mathematical issue only as a \"cleanup\", \"follow-up\", \"blocked\nitem\", or \"Phase N\" problem. State the theorem, lemma, definition, or mismatch\nin mathematical terms first; repository labels and scheduling details come\nafterward.\n\n### Multi-part work\n\nFor a chapter or theorem family spanning several PRs, use a title pattern that\nnames the mathematical region and create an umbrella **tracking issue**:\n\n```\nChapter 7 1/5: Self-improvement hypotheses\nChapter 7 2/5: Self-improvement conclusion\n...\n```\n\nAttach tracked issues as **GitHub sub-issues** of the umbrella issue so GitHub\nshows native progress, relationship navigation, and \"Tracked by #N\" links. Put descriptions in the sub-issue titles or in prose above\nthe index.\n\n### Tracking issues\n\nUse the **Tracking Issue** template (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/tracking-issue.yml`).\nLabel with `tracking`; add `chapter-tracking` for the long-lived chapter\noverview trackers. Review Checklist\n\nEvery PR touching Lean code should be reviewed against these criteria:\n\n1. **Proof correctness** -- No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.\n   Run `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\" <file>` to verify.\n\n2. **Mathlib style** -- Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and\n   `MATHLIB_doc` references. See the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review`\n   reference for the full Mathlib review guide.\n\n3. **Paper terminology** -- Public Lean names, module docstrings, declaration\n   docstrings, and documentation-visible comments should use terminology from\n   the paper and blueprint, not implementation history. See\n   [mathematical_language.md](mathematical_language.md) for the project-local\n   language rule for Lean documentation and public names. Reviewers should flag\n   names that encode historical formalization status rather than mathematical\n   content. When an old public identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR,\n   record the required migration in the issue, PR description, or an audit file\n   under [audits/](../audits/).\n   New and substantively updated audit files should follow the term norm and\n   format in\n   [audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md](../audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md).\n   Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second\n   public name.\n   Review-fix PRs must read the relevant audit files under [audits/](../audits/)\n   before changing names or prose. If an audit marks a naming migration or\n   historical-formalization term as in scope for the fix, addressing it or\n   explicitly updating the audit trail is a merge blocker.\n\n4. **Linter hygiene** -- Linter-warning cleanup must fix warnings, not mask\n   them with broad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks. See\n   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md#linter-warnings) for the project rule and the narrow\n   exception policy.\n\n5. **Type safety** -- No universe mismatches, coercion problems, or unresolved\n   metavariables.\n\n6. **Performance** -- Avoid expensive tactics on large types (e.g., `decide` on\n   `Fin 1000`). Watch for timeout-prone proof terms.\n\n7. **Modularity** -- Are new lemmas general enough to be reused? Could any be\n   upstreamed to Mathlib?\n\n8. **Documentation** -- Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.\n   Module files should have a header comment with `## References` citing the\n   relevant arXiv paper(s).\n\n9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** -- If the PR formalizes a statement\n   from the blueprint, add `\\lean{LeanDeclName}` and `\\leanok` tags to the\n   corresponding `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file. If the PR adds a public\n   auxiliary lemma that is not a named statement in the original paper, record\n   that explicitly: the Lean docstring should call it a formalization-only\n   auxiliary lemma and the blueprint should either omit it as private/internal\n   infrastructure or include it as a clearly subordinate support node connected\n   by `\\uses{...}`. See\n   [blueprint_style_guide.md](blueprint_style_guide.md#recording-formalization-only-lemmas).\n   PR descriptions and follow-up issues should cite the corresponding paper or\n   blueprint path, line, label, and a short quotation or precise paraphrase.\n   Reviewers should also check for early drift from the source: new hypotheses,\n   weakened conclusions, changed quantifier order, altered error parameters,\n   or renamed obligation structures that turn a paper theorem into a conditional\n   theorem.  If such drift appears, request a statement integrity audit before\n   reviewing the proof.  A bridge or residual hypothesis should be treated as\n   proof debt to remove, not as evidence that the paper statement has been\n   formalized.\n\n10. **Scaffolding integrity** -- If the PR introduces or modifies scaffolded\n   definitions (types, theorem statements with `sorry` proofs), verify that\n   the types and API surface align with Mathlib. Scaffolding that uses custom\n   types incompatible with Mathlib blocks future proof work. See\n   the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and\n   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md) for details.\n\n11. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** -- Review against\n   [anti_patterns.md](anti_patterns.md), which catalogues subtler failure\n   modes that pass the proof-integrity blocker checks but still fail\n   to prove the claimed mathematics: conclusion-shaped hypotheses (A1),\n   `:= rfl` definitional sleight-of-hand (A2), zero-fallback branches\n   hiding preconditions (A3), trivial default witnesses (A4),\n   Mathlib-bypass castles (A5), and external `*Statement` smuggles (A6).\n   Use the reviewer checklist at the end of that file.\n\n12. **Proof frontier integrity** -- If the PR introduces or threads structure\n   fields such as `*Input`, `*Residual`, `*BridgeInputs`, `*Witness`,\n   `*Statement`, `*Conclusion`, or `*Package`, review it against\n   [proof_frontier_review.md](proof_frontier_review.md). A PR that only\n   repackages an assumption should not be described as proving the corresponding\n   paper step; it must name the missing obligation discharger or link the native\n   sub-issue that tracks it.  For source-labelled theorems, the preferred repair\n   is to extract any usable proof content into source-faithful lemmas and\n   restore the paper-aligned statement, even if the remaining proof is a tracked\n   `sorry` during the cleanup.  For source-labelled proof gaps, also use the\n   protocol in\n   [paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex).\n\n### Semantic scaffold checklist (required for core math objects)\n\nFor semantic objects such as measurements, submeasurements, distributions,\naveraged operators, and packaged theorem outputs, reviewers should additionally\nverify:\n\n1. **Impossible states check** -- Does the structure exclude states that are\n   impossible under the paper definition?\n2. **Derived-field check** -- If a field is mathematically derived\n   (e.g. `total = ∑ a, outcome a`), is it either derived on demand or stored\n   together with an equality proof (e.g. `sum_eq_total`)?\n3. **Invariant bundling check** -- Are core invariants (positivity,\n   boundedness/normalization, completeness where applicable) encoded directly\n   in the structure or constructor, rather than deferred to downstream lemmas?\n4. **Stress-test check** -- Is at least one nontrivial theorem in scope of the\n   PR provable/stated against the scaffold without adding ad hoc assumptions?\n\nIf any answer is \"no\", treat the scaffold as unsafe and request a follow-up\nbefore broad theorem layering continues.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Lean Code Style\n\nThis project follows Mathlib conventions with project-specific additions.\n\n### Reference guides\n\nShared references (the `lean-conventions` skill of\ntexra-ai/texra-lean-skills, auto-installed via `.claude/settings.json`):\n\n- **Documentation style**: the `MATHLIB_doc` reference -- module headers,\n  docstrings, LaTeX in comments, sectioning comments.\n- **Naming conventions**: the `MATHLIB_naming` reference -- capitalization\n  rules, symbol-to-name dictionary, variable conventions.\n- **Review guide**: the `MATHLIB_pr-review` reference -- detailed examples of\n  style, documentation, location, and improvement considerations.\n\nMIPStarRE-local references:\n\n- **Mathematical language**: [mathematical_language.md](mathematical_language.md)\n  -- project-local terminology rules for Lean names and documentation.\n- **Proof integrity**: the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference plus\n  the addenda in [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md) -- blocker\n  and warning patterns for proof correctness.\n- **Blueprint style**: [blueprint_style_guide.md](blueprint_style_guide.md) --\n  notation and section conventions for the active blueprint.\n\n### Project-specific conventions\n\n**Module header**: Every `.lean` file should start with a module docstring that\nincludes:\n\n```lean\n/-!\n# Title\n\nSummary of what this file contains.\n\n## Main definitions / statements\n\n- `FooBar` : description\n- `fooBar_baz` : description\n\n## References\n\n- [arXiv:XXXX.XXXXX](https://arxiv.org/abs/XXXX.XXXXX) -- Author, *Title*\n-/\n```\n\n**Docstrings**: Required on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant\n`theorem`. Encouraged on supporting lemmas. Use Markdown; refer to Lean\nidentifiers in backticks.\n\n**Sectioning comments**: Use `/-! ### Section Title -/` to organize long files\ninto logical sections.\n\n**Variable naming**: Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` reference. For\nthis project specifically:\n- `q` for alphabet size / finite field order\n- `n`, `m` for dimension parameters\n- `σ` for strategies\n- `P` for projective measurements\n- `G` for graphs (hypercube expansion)\n\n---\n\n## 7. CI & Automation\n\nThe following workflows run automatically:\n\n| Workflow | Trigger | What it does |\n|----------|---------|-------------|\n| **Lean CI** (`pr-ci.yml` (`build` job)) | Push to `main`, PRs touching `.lean`/`lakefile.toml`/`lean-toolchain` | Runs `lake build` with Mathlib cache |\n| **PR Review** (`pr-review.yml`, `code-review` jobs) | After a successful PR CI run | Automated review for proof integrity, Mathlib style, type safety, performance, modularity, mathematical exposition, and documentation |\n| **Issue Automation** (`issue-automation.yml`) | Issue opened/labeled/closed/reopened; PR opened/merged | Classifies new issues, posts Mathlib scouting reports, keeps tracking issues current via a deterministic script (progress comments, sub-issue counts, and a ready-to-close notice when every sub-issue is resolved), and scans merged PRs for genuine deferred mathematical obligations, filing `follow-up` issues |\n| **Blueprint Lint** (`pr-ci.yml` (`blueprint-render` job)) | PRs touching blueprint files | Builds `leanblueprint pdf` / `web` to catch broken labels, undefined macros, and plasTeX errors, then runs the blueprint ↔ Lean sync checks. The active\ntrack here is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from MIP\\*=RE\n(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and NEEXP in MIP\\* (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).\n\nEvery GitHub-hosted operation of the parent workflow is replaced by a local\nequivalent that *executes* here.
