The service gate merged it as\n`81148545f0752ec09b3efe88332b49bb771312be`. The primary used a finite\nsame-inode telemetry boundary rather than waiting for unrelated writers. The\nmerged continuation then consumed the preserved PR #400 CODE and PROSE\nresponses and published canonical failure review `5147250926` with seven\nunresolved findings. It launched no new model turn, edited no response or\nsource, and released the old reviewer and source holds. PR #400 remains\nineligible to merge until its isolated repair proceeds through normal checked\npublication, CI, and fresh independent review.\n\n## 2026-09-09 - Reviewed merge trains (issue #502)\n\n**Trigger:** the 09:05Z meta decision in `results/telemetry/design-decisions.md`\n(D1, issue #502) records that each single-PR merge invalidates other refreshed\nheads. See the issue #502 development entry in `results/telemetry/events.md`.\n\n**Change:** add `pr_train.py`, a non-publishing integration mode in `ci.sh`,\nand a train-manifest check after `checked-push.sh` preflight. Reuse the existing\nmember gates and CI steps; replace only individual-head base ancestry with\nmandatory combined-commit validation. Preserve exact-head independent review,\ndependency gates, checked fast-forward publication, and the full-build lock.\nCI step bodies stop on command failure; cache warming cannot start a nested\nfull build. `issues-prs.md` documents the operator-owned invocation and recovery.\n\n**Expected effect:** two or more ready PRs share one integration build and CI\nrun without losing a member's evidence or silently discarding accepted work.\nActivation remains subject to independent review and daemon-owner deployment.\n"}, "8bda0fc86b2fcee9d1f7bd011957d992432743799eeb51f43ff6d0d161e08629": {"encoding": "utf8", "content": "# Protocol: issues and pull requests\n\nNormative for the GitHub-backed issue and PR lifecycle and the automation in\n`local/bin/`; read `local/protocols/meta.md` first. The repository is\n`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`, and GitHub is the **single source of truth** for\nissues, PRs, CI and review evidence, and merges; CI and reviews still *execute*\nhere and publish their results there. No active `issues/` or `prs/` tree, no\nshadow record, no write-through cache, no offline mutation mode: a GitHub error\nfails the operation, never a local success (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01).\n\n## 1. Records, names, tools\n\nIssues and PRs are GitHub's, identified by their numbers — no zero-padded ids,\nno frontmatter. Parent/child structure is the native sub-issue relation\n(`POST …/issues/{parent}/sub_issues`), one parent per issue exactly as the\nretired `parent:` scalar allowed; discussion is comments; labels come from the\nrepository (`list-labels`, paginated), so `local/labels.yml` is retired and a\nlabel absent from GitHub is reported, never invented.\n`pr_open.py --issue N` inherits only its explicit descriptive-label allowlist\nfrom issue N, unions it with explicit `--label` values, and adds those labels\nwithout removing existing PR labels. Scheduling, approval and owner-state\nlabels are never inherited. Before push, creation/adoption requires at least\none descriptive label, supplied explicitly, inherited, or already on the PR;\notherwise the command explains how the operator can classify the change.\nGitHub still validates label existence; the allowlist is an inheritance policy,\nnot a replacement registry. Backfills use the same additive API and inspect\nthe actual change when the source issue itself is unlabeled. Briefs (the design record\nper issue) live in `local/briefs/`: agent input, not lifecycle state.\n\nPrerequisites between issues are **GitHub issue dependencies**\n(`GET`/`POST …/issues/{n}/dependencies/blocked_by`), one edge per prerequisite.\nThe edge is retained even when the prerequisite closes, so reopening it restores the block.\nA prerequisite carried by a pull request is the packet issue that PR closes. The\n\"Dependencies\" bullets in an issue body are commentary on those edges, never\nthe record. A packet is **ready** when it is an open leaf of the tracker tree\nand every issue blocking it is closed; `local/bin/ready_packets.py` computes\nthat list, and the operator launches lanes from it rather than from a\nhand-kept order or a dependency table in a comment (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-04).\nEstablish or adopt each edge with\n`local/bin/gh_common.py add-blocked-by ISSUE PREREQUISITE`. The command first\nreads the edge, makes at most one mutation, and re-reads after an ambiguous\nfailure; it is therefore safe to repeat. Record closed prerequisites too.\n\nEvery GitHub call goes through `local/bin/gh_common.py` — a module for Python\ncallers, and for the shell scripts a CLI (`pr-view`, `post-status`,\n`latest-statuses`, `ensure-pr-comment`, `post-review`, `merge-pr`,\n`issue-create`, `add-blocked-by`, `issue-close`, `snapshot`, …; `--help` lists\nthem) owning CLI discovery, repository resolution, API version headers,\nbounded retry of transient failures and the exit-2-with-stderr convention.\nNothing else shells out to `gh`. `issue_new.py`, `issue_close.py`, `pr_open.py`,\n`ci.sh`, `review.sh`, `autofix.sh`, `pr_merge.py`, `github-sync.sh` take GitHub\nnumbers; `track.py`, `validate_tree.py` and `export_issues.py` are deleted.\n\nEvery repository-owned branch publication runs through `checked-push.sh` with\none explicit `refs/heads/...:refs/heads/...` mapping.  The helper reads the\nremote tip with a short `ls-remote`, resolves the local ref's registered\nworktree, and refuses a checkout whose HEAD or working tree differs from the\ncaptured commit.  It runs that checkout's `.githooks/pre-push` against the exact\nref tuple before starting `receive-pack`, then pushes the captured commit under\nan exact remote-tip lease.  The native hook performs a short defense-in-depth\ncomparison when selected, while the helper's lease makes a moved remote ref fail\nclosed even when that hook is stale or absent.  A caller's explicit\n`MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1` remains the documented emergency bypass.  It skips\nvalidation only: implicit tag following stays disabled, so publication remains\nlimited to the explicit branch mapping.\n\n`github-sync.sh [ref ...]` takes branch names (default `main`), not a `push`\nsubcommand. It retains the post-publication record snapshot. When an explicitly\nrequested/default main push succeeded and the snapshot created a new telemetry\ncommit, it checked-pushes main once more without creating another snapshot.\nBranch-only calls never implicitly publish main. Snapshot reads remain best-effort;\nsnapshot commit or final publication failure returns nonzero and leaves the\npreserved local state for the operator to recover.\n\nEvery merge of `github/main` or a stack parent into an issue branch runs the\nmerge-loss guard before the merge commit is created. The guard compares the\npending index with `HEAD`, `MERGE_HEAD`, and every best merge base. It refuses\nan incoming path that disappeared without a branch-side deletion and an\nincoming-only entry restored wholesale to the unchanged branch blob. Paths\nrecorded by Git as conflicts remain resolution decisions. The\n`reference-transaction` hook checks an automatic merge's commit object before\nthe branch ref moves; `pre-commit` checks the pending index for a merge\ncommitted later. Neither path permits `MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS` to bypass this\ncheck. A lane checking an existing merge uses the primary checkout's\n`local/bin/merge_loss_guard.py --repo <worktree> --commit <merge>` so a stale\nbranch copy cannot weaken the audit.\n\n* Branches: `issue-<github-number>-<slug>`, or `codex/issue-<number>-<slug>`\n  from an agent; `pr_open.py` rejects what `git check-ref-format` would.\n* Titles, slugs and branch names are **bracket-free**: bot-generated branch\n  names inherit those characters and \"`]` breaks part of the PR automation\n  stack\" (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124). A `:` in a *title* is fine\n  (`Tracking: …`), but not in a branch.\n* `autofix.sh`'s automated fix commits keep the exact subject prefixes\n  `[codex-auto-fix]` and `[codex-review-fix]`; its iteration counter and the\n  review skip key on them.  Operator and worker repairs use plain\n  `fix(review): …` / `fix(ci): …` subjects so the reviewer sees them.\n* `Closes #N` / `Fixes #N` auto-closes the issue on merge, `Addresses #N` does\n  not (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:61-62) — and the numbers being GitHub's, that\n  footer is now literally what GitHub itself reads.\n\n## 2. Evidence contracts\n\nAll evidence binds to the **exact head SHA** (DESIGN.md invariant 2).\n\n**Commit statuses.** Ten canonical contexts, posted by `post-status`: one\n`local-ci/<step>` per CI step (`build`, `blueprint-render`, `paper-gaps`,\n`blueprint-sync`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`,\n`statement-origin`), plus `local-ci/summary` and `local-review/summary`.\n`ci.sh` posts `pending` before each gate step and `success | failure | error`\nafter it; a gated-out step is a `success` saying it was skipped. The gate reads\nthe *latest* status per context (`latest-statuses`), never GitHub's combined\nstatus, silent as that is about contexts never posted. The run manifest is one\nPR comment marked `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, kept current by\n`ensure-pr-comment`: evidence for humans, while the statuses are the gate.\n\n**Review verdict.** One `COMMENT` review per head SHA, bound to `commit_id`,\ncarrying `<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`, the findings ledger, and the\nline `VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=…, prose=…)`.\nUnchecked findings are ledger lines matching `^\\s*[-*]\\s*\\[ \\]`; clean means\n`APPROVED`, or `COMMENTED` with none of them. Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT`\ntoo — a **single account** cannot approve its own pull request, so the review\nevent carries no authority — and adverseness travels in `local-review/summary`\n(`failure` for unresolved findings), which is the gate's review evidence.\n\n**Adjudication** (review.md §12) is a PR comment whose body starts with\n`ADJUDICATION` and contains `head=<SHA>` for the current head, one disposition\nline per remaining finding; `--adjudicated` takes nothing else.\n\n**Idempotency.** Every publishing step is **at most one mutation**: a paginated\nread finds the stable marker first and adopts that record instead of duplicating\nit (`commentOnce`, issue-automation.yml:403-417, now guarding retries rather than\nwebhook redelivery); an ambiguous write stays pending for adoption.\n\n## 3. The merge gate\n\nSingle-PR merges use `pr_merge.py <number>`; reviewed batches use `pr_train.py`\nas described below. Workers never merge or publish main directly. A single-PR\nmerge is a REST `PUT …/pulls/{n}/merge` with the exact\n`sha` guard, issued by `gh_common.merge_pr` and verified against the merge\ncommit's topology (two parents, the frozen head second), behind seven gates\nthat refuse by default:\n\n1. the PR is open, unmerged and not a draft (`draft is False`, not merely\n   falsy), and reports a head SHA, a head ref and a base ref;\n2. the primary worktree is clean and on the base, and the local branch tip\n   equals the GitHub head SHA — the merge must be of the bytes built here;\n3. all eight `local-ci/<step>` contexts plus `local-ci/summary` are `success` on\n   that exact SHA; a **missing** context blocks, because GitHub's combined state\n   reads `success` for a commit carrying no statuses at all;\n4. that SHA's marker-bound `COMMENT` review (or one carried forward per\n   review.md §13) carries `VERDICT: APPROVED`, or\n   `COMMENTED` with zero unchecked findings, **and** `local-review/summary` is\n   `success` there;\n5. no `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review stands on that head, from anyone;\n6. no live fix lock for the branch (`locks/fix-<branch>.lock`, running holder);\n   the count of `merge-base..head` commits whose subject starts with a §1 fix\n   prefix is printed for the record and is not a gate;\n7. every issue the PR body closes — all nine of GitHub's closing keywords, not\n   just `Closes` — has no open sub-issue left.\n\n`--adjudicated` waives gate 4's adverse verdict and nothing else, and only when\nan exact-head `ADJUDICATION` comment backs it; gate 5 is never adjudicable.\n\nAfterwards a best-effort, non-fatal tail fast-forwards local `main` to the\nremote merge commit; branch and worktree cleanup keeps its safeguards (local\ndirt defers it with a warning).\n\n### Reviewed merge trains\n\nAfter independent review and deployment, the daemon/operator may invoke\n`local/bin/pr_train.py N M [K ...]` from the clean primary checkout at\n`github/main`. Development and tests use fixture repositories exclusively.\nEvery member passes the existing open, local-tip, exact-head CI, independent\nreview, changes-requested, fix-lock, and dependency gates. Repeat\n`--adjudicated N` only for members with the existing exact-head adjudication\nrecord. A precondition failure refuses the entire batch and names the member.\nThe individual-head base-ancestry requirement is replaced by mandatory CI of\nthe combined commit; member review evidence is neither copied nor rewritten.\n\nThe tool creates `train/<UTC-stamp>` and a private worktree under the runtime\ncache, merging frozen member SHAs with two-parent merge commits in argument\norder. A conflict aborts only that merge, verifies restoration of the accepted\ntrain, and drops that member; fewer than two accepted members refuses the batch.\nThe primary merge-loss guard checks each accepted merge. Existing developer\nbranches and worktrees are preserved. Failed train worktrees remain for diagnosis.\n\n`ci.sh --integration-head SHA --worktree PATH --base SHA` runs all eight steps\nagainst the combined commit, using one locked build of `MIPStarRE.QPBT` and\n`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`. It rejects skip flags and dirty or moved train\nheads, and publishes no PR evidence. Its manifest and logs stay in the runtime\ncache. Bootstrap and build telemetry are transferred to the primary telemetry\nfiles after publication or refusal so their appends cannot dirty the primary\nduring gating. CI warming uses `--no-build` to avoid a nested build lock, and\nstep execution stops at its first failing command.\n\nPublication uses `checked-push.sh --train-manifest PATH` with one explicit\ntrain-to-main ref mapping. After preflight, it rechecks the combined CI manifest,\nmember gates and heads, primary cleanliness, and frozen main; the existing exact\nremote-tip lease protects the final fast-forward. Hook bypass is forbidden.\nGitHub recognizes included PRs by ancestry; the tool closes no issue by hand.\nIt posts one idempotent train comment per member, records one merge event,\nfast-forwards local main and its origin alias, and removes only the train branch\nand worktree. A failure after publication is reported as such and requires\noperator reconciliation; it must not be retried as a new merge. Deployment and\ndaemon wiring remain separate from development of this tool (issue #502).\n\n### Main-cycle integration checkpoint\n\nThe active owner service records, at each bounded tick, the local `main` SHA,\nthe readable remote `refs/heads/main` SHA, primary cleanliness, transport\nresult, and the age and exact head of the oldest CI-and-review-eligible open\nPR. A dirty primary, remote mismatch, unavailable transport, active fix or\ntransaction lock, missing configured Space allocation or external-zero gate, or a stale\ncandidate is\na HOLD reason; it is never silently converted into a merge attempt. After a\nsuccessful daemon-owned merge, the service re-reads remote `main` and records\nthe new SHA before the next tick. The service may invoke `pr_merge.py` only as\nits daemon-owned final action after these checks; workers never merge directly.\nEach tick has bounded Git/GitHub reads and records failures as HOLD rather than\nexiting the loop. The cadence is monotonic: work time is subtracted from the\nconfigured interval (default 300 seconds). Candidate records distinguish stale\nexact-head PRs from fresh actionable PRs; `pr_age_s` is PR creation age, while\neligibility onset remains unknown unless separately observed.\n\n## 4. Untrusted text\n\nIssue and PR bodies are untrusted data, and **more** so now that they arrive\nfrom GitHub: anyone with repository access, and every imported external report,\nwrites the fields that are echoed into generated markdown and interpolated into\nagent prompts. All three parent workflows sanitized before interpolation, and\n`wf_util.sanitize` is that step ported: strip control characters, break fenced\ncode with zero-width spaces, truncate to 200 characters for titles and 5000 for\nbodies (issue-automation.yml:122-128).\n\nEvery LLM hook in `local/bin` carries the same four requirements: gate on\n`MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED != \"false\"`; read prompts from committed main\n(`git show main:…`), never the branch under review (DESIGN.md:76-77); frame\nsanitized text as data that must not be followed; and filter any model-proposed\nlabel through the repository's label list. `audit_stale_issues.py` additionally\nkeeps its path-traversal rejection for externally sourced citations.\n\n## 5. Environment, snapshot, archive\n\n`MIPSTARRE_GH` is the path to `gh` (else `PATH`, else the documented user-local\nlocation); `MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO` overrides the `owner/name` otherwise read\nfrom the `github` remote; `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP` (default 5) bounds `autofix.sh`'s\nown loop only — the merge gate does not read it — and is operator-tunable with\nthe reason recorded in `results/telemetry/events.md`, unlike\n`MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE` (the pre-commit budget), the one owner-gated control\nin the layer. `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` and\n`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` keep kill-switch semantics (DESIGN.md:73-75).\n\n`github-sync.sh` pushes explicit refs and writes an atomic, paginated read-only\nsnapshot of open issues and PRs to `results/telemetry/github-snapshot/`\n(and, since the push goes through `checked-push.sh`, commits that snapshot and\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` to the primary checkout so the next publish\nfinds a clean tree)\n(`open-issues.json`, `open-pulls.json`, `metadata.json`; PRs filtered out of the\nissue endpoint) — audit and recovery telemetry, never lifecycle input. The\nretired trees stay archived under `results/telemetry/registry-archive/` (commit\nc8f1999): read-only research data, never edited or read as active input.\n\n## 6. Owner inbox and mathematical-gap escalation\n\nPinned issue #26 is the owner inbox: it receives only decisions that require\nthe human owner. A source statement found to be mathematically false does not\ngo there first. Following the availability report on #26 and the September 6\nowner decision, main selects Astra Ultra for the mathematical-gap lane through\n`MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-6-astra local/bin/dispatch.sh --role mathfix --effort ultra`\nor the shared native protocol in `sessions.md`.\nHistorical owner-launched Fable measurements remain unchanged. Every request or\ndispatch carries the exact source path, label and line range; the counterexample\nor obstruction; the paper-gap note; the relevant blueprint dependency graph and\nLean consumers; and the cumulative session count and elapsed working time.\n\nA correction is adopted only when it meets all four conditions below.\n\n1. **Correctness:** the known counterexample no longer applies, adversarial\n   checks find no replacement counterexample, and a mathematical proof sketch\n   derives the corrected conclusion from its explicit hypotheses using cited\n   source results.\n2. **Sufficiency:** every use in the paper and every dependent node in the\n   blueprint graph remains justified; checking only the first Lean consumer is\n   insufficient.\n3. **Minimality:** the correction is the closest sufficient statement to the\n   source, with no unnecessary hypothesis or weakened conclusion and no change\n   to the source semantics; definition or game corrections require an explicit\n   faithfulness audit and independent mathematical review.\n4. **Lean convergence:** the corrected statement type-checks and all affected\n   downstream consumers compile. Lean success alone does not establish the\n   preceding three conditions.\n\nThe operator iterates mathematics and Lean for at most ten `mathfix` sessions\nor about one and a half working days per gap, whichever comes first. The budget\nis shared across the historical owner-launched Fable lane and the Astra lane; a\nmodel or telemetry change does not reset it. Main decides mathematical\ncorrections with the preceding evidence and independent review, including\ndefinition/game corrections that preserve the intended source semantics;\nchanging the project goal is outside that authority. If the current authorized\nbudget expires, stop that lane and record the attempted statements,\ncounterexamples, proof sketches and unresolved consumers on #27 and in the gap\nnote. Do not reset attempts or working time. Use #26 only for an owner-only\npermission, credential, access or scope/resource grant; mathematical difficulty\nalone is not an owner decision. An already-posted #26 item waits for the owner\nunless the owner explicitly returns it to main.\n\nAn adopted correction follows the ordinary CI and independent-review gates. The\noperator announces it in one line on progress log #27 and records it in the\npaper-gap note, `results/telemetry/events.md`, and\n`results/telemetry/design-decisions.md`. That announcement informs the owner; it\nis not a request for a decision.\n"}, "20be34db86d5ce015e31b02c65f7e6b07a948d33d169003a88a91df5627b621c": {"encoding": "utf8", "content": "test_member_moving_at_transport_start_refuses (scripts.tests.test_pr_train.TrainTests) ... ok\n\n----------------------------------------------------------------------\nRan 1 test in 7.803s\n\nOK\n"}, "8faf0df92e45456fb3729029f0385476312412fcbbd4aae3a9cc40e0ebba1871": {"encoding": "utf8", "content": "# PR507 publication adjudication, 2026-09-17\n\n**Disposition: genuine remaining in-scope blocker. Original F1 is only partially\nfixed; retain the operator hold. F2 is fixed.** This packet is technical evidence\nfor MAIN, not a new review round, posted approval, or authorization to change scope.\n\nReviewed head: `55e573949537f392c6e0d427af1dca6783d2474c`.\nTrusted policy/personas: `d6caa66c8cb36ffd0c0c7c141cda7d0c12b4a325`.\nWorktree: `/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-502-reviewed-merge-train`.\nThe checkout was clean at admission and after the tests. The trusted pin is an\nancestor of admission main `4dcecb70f7094dc2be90b315435224d2336e7a3c`; their only\nchanged path is `results/telemetry/owner-sessions.jsonl`.\nThe brief was read in full before work. First recorded UTC check: 14:47:33;\nabsolute deadline: 14:57:05. Requested hardness: contested publication-control\ninvariant after reviewer disagreement and an isolated Git transaction race.\n\n## Original contract and prior dispositions\n\n1. [Issue502](https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/502) requires unchanged\n   per-PR current-head CI/review/dependency preconditions, integration of the\n   accepted PR branches, and checked fast-forward publication. It does not itself\n   specify an advertisement-to-commit linearization point. The original design at\n   `e1dd7bb0`, `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`, describes frozen member SHAs,\n   post-preflight member rechecks, and a main lease. The 09:05 decision at the\n   trusted pin, `results/telemetry/design-decisions.md:67`, authorizes the train\n   through review; it supplies no exception to current-head guards.\n2. Trusted `local/protocols/issues-prs.md:104` binds evidence to exact heads;\n   lines 137-140 retain the existing single-PR REST merge's exact-SHA guard.\n   These establish evidence identity and the existing comparison at merge, not\n   an already-deployed multi-ref transaction mechanism. Exact reviewed content\n   and equality of the live member ref at publication are distinct properties.\n3. [Original review5194195608](https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/pull/507#pullrequestreview-5194195608)\n   at `26ecf158b1e03248964f8634d42087135cc61be6` expressly requires an atomic\n   server-side guard covering every member ref, or equivalent, **and** a test for\n   movement at transport start. Passing that requested test alone does not meet\n   the separately stated server-side invariant.\n4. Crucially, MAIN already accepted that interpretation in\n   [comment5660459454](https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/pull/507#issuecomment-5660459454)\n   on September 14. It reports reproduction with leased no-op refspecs, keeps F1\n   blocking, and explicitly rejects client rechecks or a frozen-snapshot contract\n   as substitutes. It preserves issue502 as the obligation and authorizes no new\n   transport framework, protection change, repair allowance, or deployment.\n   This is direct prior disposition, not a stronger invariant invented here.\n5. [Review5236849687](https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/pull/507#pullrequestreview-5236849687)\n   approves this exact head with no findings, while acknowledging the remaining\n   advertisement-to-commit window. Its factual timing observation is correct;\n   its conclusion that F1 is resolved conflicts with the original finding and\n   MAIN's recorded disposition. Candidate protocol prose cannot settle that\n   conflict by silently narrowing the contract. Trusted `meta.md` requires an\n   explicit recorded amendment; `review.md` permits operator adjudication but\n   does not turn an unproved invariant into a fixed finding.\n\nThe operational invariant in dispute is: in the transaction advancing main\nfrom base B to tested train T, every included live member ref must still equal\nits admitted reviewed SHA H_i; otherwise publication must fail without changing\nmain or rewinding a member. This need not keep members frozen after the commit.\nCurrent code preserves reviewed content in T, but does not enforce the member\nequalities at that transaction.\n\n## What the candidate enforces\n\n- `pr_train.py:104-137` rechecks member gates, exact identities, train contents,\n  combined CI, primary cleanliness and remote refs before transport. It returns\n  the members, and lines 290-296 emit them for checked-push.\n- `checked-push.sh:147-199` adds explicit member leases and same-SHA refspecs to\n  the atomic push. A member whose **advertised** value differs from the expected\n  SHA causes client rejection of the atomic push. The existing focused test\n  demonstrates this and passed in this session.\n- When advertised member values match, Git marks their refspecs up to date and\n  sends no update commands for them. The only command in this experiment is\n  B -> T for main. Atomicity and main's old-value comparison cover that command;\n  they do not add predicates for refs absent from the command list.\n- Local PR locks, another `ls-remote`, another client hook, or a post-push read\n  cannot supply the missing server transaction predicate. A post-push read may\n  diagnose a discrepancy after main has already advanced.\n\nThe docstring at `pr_train.py:108-110` overclaims the implemented guarantee by\nrequiring current member refs when the remote commits. The more serious issue is the synthetic “official report” fixture: it invents `status/stage/phase/source/comparator` semantics that are not tied to any identified upstream producer. I’m tracing the official producer and field meanings now.

    29	  and in dependency order, every declaration in the comparator-relevant
    30	  closure of the statement of `mainFormal` (111 declarations, ~1200 lines),
    31	  then states the theorem with `sorry`.  It is the entire human audit
    32	  surface.
    33	- `Solution.lean` there imports this library, which proves the theorem under
    34	  the same fully-qualified names; no bridging lemmas are needed.
    35	- Its CI runs the comparator (real landrun sandbox, nanoda external kernel,
    36	  `lean4checker` re-check) on every push and weekly.
    37	
    38	## What this repository contributes
    39	
    40	1. **Environment alignment.**  Comparator compares, constant by constant, the
    41	   full kernel closure of the statement — types, definition bodies, and the
    42	   proofs embedded in them — so `Challenge.lean` must elaborate to
    43	   bit-identical terms.  Every module contributing a declaration to the
    44	   closure therefore uses the full `import Mathlib` (directly or through
    45	   `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/ParametersBase.lean` /
    46	   `MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`), so tactic elaboration sees
    47	   the same environment as the Mathlib-only `Challenge.lean`.  The four
    48	   modules with direct Mathlib imports carry a comment saying not to narrow
    49	   them.  (Measured impact: only 14 modules that did not already see full
    50	   Mathlib through `Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean` gained it.)
    51	2. **Regeneration tooling.**  `scripts/comparator/` holds the closure
    52	   extractor (a Lean metaprogram mirroring comparator's `runForUsedConsts`)
    53	   and the assembler that produce `Challenge.lean`.  After changing any
    54	   definition in the closure: regenerate per `scripts/comparator/README.md`,
    55	   copy the result into LDT-comparator, and bump its library pin.
    56	
    57	## Checklist against the official *Validating Proofs* guide
    58	
    59	| Level | Requirement | Status |
    60	|---|---|---|
    61	| 2 | `#print axioms` shows only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` | `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean`; also enforced by comparator's `permitted_axioms` |
    62	| 3 | `lean4checker --fresh` re-check | `lean4checker: true` in the comparator repo's lean-action step |
    63	| 4 | Statement written in a trusted environment, separate from proof code | `Challenge.lean` imports only Mathlib (CI-enforced grep); separate repo, library pinned by commit |
    64	| 4 | Sandboxed build + export + kernel replay | official comparator binary (pinned to the toolchain tag), real landrun in CI |
    65	| 4 | External checker in addition to the Lean kernel | `enable_nanoda = true` (pinned nanoda tag); local macOS runs use `./verify.sh --fake-landrun` which disables it |
    66	| 5 | No native evaluation (`Lean.trustCompiler`, `decide +native`) | excluded by `permitted_axioms` — comparator rejects any extra axiom |
    67	| — | Statement review: custom notation and type classes must not obscure meaning | `Challenge.lean` uses no custom notation; review of it is the human step |
    68	
    69	Deliberate deviations from the comparator README's adversarial setup, per its
    70	own guidance for trusted trees: the `systemd-run` landrun-escape guard is
    71	omitted and prebuilt `.lake` artifacts are reused, because both modules come
    72	from a trusted checkout rather than an untrusted submitter.
    73	
    74	Residual trust: Lean's logical soundness, comparator's own plumbing, sandbox
    75	security, simultaneous bugs in all checkers, and human error in
    76	`Challenge.lean` itself — keep that file short, notation-free, and reviewed.
    77	
    78	## The QPBT challenge
    79	
    80	The QPBT challenge is prepared for the separate repository
    81	**[QPBT-comparator](https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator)**.  Its current
    82	configuration supplies these four theorem names to one comparator run:
    83	
    84	- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one` (`lem:pauli-completeness`);
    85	- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness` (`lem:ld-soundness`);
    86	- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` (`thm:pauli`); and
    87	- `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` (`cor:pauli-binary`).
    88	
    89	The checked-in generated tree is `scripts/comparator/expected/qpbt/`.  It has a
    90	root `Challenge.lean` and thirty Mathlib-only mirror modules under `Challenge/`,
    91	one for each contributing library module.  The root states all four targets
    92	with `sorry`; the drift guard regenerates and byte-compares the complete tree
    93	with `--challenge qpbt`.
    94	
    95	### Current verification status
    96	
    97	On September 21, 2026 UTC (September 22, 2026 JST), official comparator
    98	[run 35638601720](https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator/actions/runs/35638601720)
    99	([job 106462118372](https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator/actions/runs/35638601720/job/106462118372))
   100	completed successfully at QPBT-comparator commit
   101	`360402fdf4a39399f94331452d6e5d0a35c144be`.  Both `lakefile.toml` and the
   102	manifest's `rev` and `inputRev` pinned library commit
   103	`ecb97d1f66eec1e6fad964f144f78b91ce1fab36`, the merged-main result of PR 671.
   104	The run's configuration named all four targets above, enabled nanoda, and
   105	permitted exactly `propext`, `Quot.sound`, and `Classical.choice`.
   106	Preliminary run 35621468975 at unmerged library commit
   107	`a3683e9b75da4aeb52174af2cccacfde606361ce` is not evidence for this record.
   108	
   109	The workflow used Lean `v4.32.0` and the official comparator tag at
   110	`07bc4ea40f2266dcb861820a2ec1fa3244ed307f`, with landrun pinned at
   111	`c91b41ac6cb180e2fdcb989408dcde34449bd8b0` and nanoda pinned at
   112	`f58f2f6d535e189a40fcb02ede8eb95f97a92d37`.  It invoked `./verify.sh` without
   113	`--fake-landrun`, required the real `landrun` executable, and ran
   114	`lake env comparator comparator.json`.  The retained log exports all four
   115	theorem names from both `Challenge` and `Solution`, then records that the nanoda
   116	kernel and Lean's default kernel each accept the solution.  This establishes
   117	equality of the complete union of the four statement closures at the verified
   118	library commit.  Before that run, PR 671 either eliminated the earlier private
   119	and compiler-generated blockers from the closure or made the affected closure
   120	declarations public.  The successful comparison verifies the resulting current
   121	closure; it did not compare those former blockers under their old names.
   122	
   123	The completion gate reads the following record.  For an exact-head QPBT
   124	completion claim, C5's delegated evidence must include a passing drift check
   125	from CI on that same commit; carrying this documentation record alone does not
   126	select the comparator build step.
   127	
   128	<!-- completion-gate: track=qpbt -->
   129	- challenge-repository: https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator
   130	- verified-library-commit: ecb97d1f66eec1e6fad964f144f78b91ce1fab36
   131	- expected-challenge: scripts/comparator/expected/qpbt
   132	- drift-check: scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py
   133	- covered-theorems: MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness, MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit, MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one, MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness
   134	
   135	Comparator acceptance is a closure-equality result, not a source-faithfulness
   136	certificate.  It does not prove that the trusted challenge faithfully states
   137	the QPBT paper, settle completion criteria C3 or C4, perform the final artifact
   138	build, or establish that the QPBT track is complete.  Any later change to the
   139	statement closure requires regeneration, a passing drift check, and a new
   140	official comparator run before this verification claim can be advanced.
   141	
   142	There is a narrower historical result.  At commit
   143	`4aec9ebedf6ca401e3f2d7b4bd90bd565d38f90d`, the split challenge configured
   144	only `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` and
   145	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit`.  On that exact two-target configuration,
   146	`./verify.sh --fake-landrun` reported acceptance.  Fake landrun disables nanoda,
   147	and that run did not include `exists_spcc_value_one` or `exists_ld_soundness`, so
   148	it is not evidence for the current four-target challenge.
   149	
   150	### Environment alignment for QPBT
   151	
   152	Comparator compares the full kernel closure constant by constant, so each
   153	Mathlib-only challenge module must elaborate to bit-identical terms.  The
   154	library and generator use the following alignment measures:
   155	
   156	1. **Full Mathlib imports.**  Four closure modules -
   157	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Subspaces.lean`,
   158	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Coefficients.lean`,
   159	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/LowDegreeCode.lean`, and
   160	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Lines.lean` - use the full `import Mathlib`, so tactic
   161	   elaboration sees the same environment as the challenge modules.  Other
   162	   closure modules receive Mathlib through existing shared imports.
   163	2. **Public closure members.**  A `private` declaration's real name is qualified
   164	   by its defining module (`_private.<module>.0.<name>`), so a challenge module
   165	   cannot re-declare it under the library's name.  Closure members needed by the
   166	   challenge were therefore made public without changing their statements,
   167	   bodies, or proof scripts.
   168	3. **Named local instances.**  The group and decidable-equality instances for
   169	   the Galois group in `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/FieldBasis.lean` have explicit
   170	   names.  This avoids generated names that encode the defining module.
   171	4. **Mirrored module partition.**  Lean caches nested proof and `match`
   172	   auxiliaries per module, names them after the first declaration in that module
   173	   that needs them, and limits instance synthesis to the module's imports.  The
   174	   QPBT challenge therefore mirrors the source module partition and import
   175	   graph.  This behavior is selected by `"split": true` in
   176	   `scripts/comparator/challenges/qpbt.json`; `assemble_challenge.py --split-dir`
   177	   writes the tree under `scripts/comparator/expected/qpbt/`.
   178	
   179	The split layout also avoids adding QPBT-specific global instance wrappers to
   180	`MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`.  The baseline regression described
   181	in `scripts/comparator/README.md` independently protects the current checked-in
   182	LDT challenge fixture.  During this module-conversion pilot, that baseline
   183	received a one-time, provenance-only reset because the new module and
   184	public-section headers shifted two generated `-- source:` line comments; the
   185	LDT challenge declarations and target statement were unchanged.
   186	
   187	No public statement of any of the four targets changed as part of this
   188	comparator alignment.  The official run above established comparator equality
   189	for the verified merged-main library commit.
   190	
   191	The "do not narrow this import" notes on the shared base modules
   192	(`MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/ParametersBase.lean`,
   193	`MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/Distribution.lean`,
   194	`MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`) still name only `mainFormal`,
   195	and deliberately so: those modules contribute to both closures, and adding a
   196	line to a module docstring shifts every declaration below it, which would
   197	rewrite the `-- source:` provenance comments of the checked-in LDT challenge.
   198	They are covered by this section instead.
   199	
   200	### Regenerating and auditing
   201	
   202	Regeneration is the pipeline in `scripts/comparator/README.md` with
   203	`--challenge qpbt`.  After an intentional change to any definition in the
   204	closure: regenerate, copy the expected file into QPBT-comparator as
   205	`Challenge.lean` and `Challenge/`, bump the `rev` pin in its `lakefile.toml`
   206	and `lake-manifest.json` to the library commit they were generated from, and
   207	run its `./verify.sh`.
   208	
   209	What the human must audit, and what no tool can check: that the challenge
   210	modules really state the intended theorems.  Concretely, that
   211	the Pauli basis test it defines — `pauliQuestionDistribution`,
   212	`pauliWinPredicate`, `pauliBasisTest` — is the test of the paper; that
   213	`deltaQld` is the paper's error functional; that `PauliSoundnessWitness` and
   214	`QubitSoundnessWitness` package isometries and an auxiliary state without
   215	smuggling in a hypothesis; and that `Strategy.value` and the operator
   216	distances mean what their names claim.  Agreement of the remaining declarations
   217	was established by the four-target comparator run above; their intended
   218	mathematical meaning and agreement with the cited paper remain matters for
   219	source comparison and review.
   220	
   221	## Benchmark use
   222	
   223	The same statement is submission-ready for
   224	[leanprover/lean-eval](https://github.com/leanprover/lean-eval) (the official
   225	comparator-based benchmark behind [lean-lang.org/eval](https://lean-lang.org/eval/)):
   226	port the statement module to lean-eval's toolchain, tag the theorem
   227	`@[eval_problem]`, add a `manifests/problems/<id>.toml` (`holes`, `submitter`,
   228	`source`, `informal_solution`), and open a PR to lean-eval.  Large
   229	self-contained statement preludes have precedent there (the knot-theory
   230	problems ship a 23 KB trusted `ChallengeDeps.lean`).  Solvers edit only
   231	`Submission.lean`; scoring is comparator acceptance, with submissions run by
   232	the Lean FRO's hosted pipeline.

1	### Motivation
     2	Palomar preparation #743 requires schema-valid metadata and a recorded local check of every mechanical requirement. These can be prepared while library conversion proceeds, then validated on the final compact Challenge and pinned library.
     3	
     4	### Scope
     5	In the fresh QPBT-comparator preparation clone, draft formalization.yaml from the current v0.4 schema and repository evidence, and add a small local validator with an evidence-report command. Do not change Challenge, Solution, the library dependency pin, or the official comparator workflow yet. Keep existing repository and license facts truthful. State that the work is AI-generated, without human review beyond the owner's decisions; the owner is Ruixuan Deng. Every uncertain credit or submission-authority field belongs in the final owner note, not an invented assertion.
     6	
     7	The validator must cover the selected root layout, pinned/supported toolchain and matching Mathlib revision, manifest and immutable canonical library pin, exactly one root license, module headers and line caps (including the separately declared substantive library), Challenge bytes/lines and trusted import closure, comparator declaration configuration and permitted axioms/NanoDa, and metadata schema. Distinguish source scans from authoritative kernel/comparator evidence; require actual evidence for proof/axiom claims. Preserve a deterministic report whose inputs are bound by file hashes so adding the report does not create a self-referential commit-SHA requirement. Use the existing official tools or public schemas where practical; no framework or new service.
     8	
     9	### Acceptance
    10	Focused meaningful fixture checks and schema validation; the current old split Challenge is expected to fail Palomar limits, and must not be reported green. Commit a draft checkpoint, return exact paths and pending integration requirements.      1	# Briefing for the MAIN SESSION — prepare the QPBT for Palomar (owner aim, 2026-10-01)
     2	
     3	Written on 2026-10-01 by the owner's Claude session on the Mac, on the owner's direct instruction
     4	"dispatch a codex main on ghz + 3 sub slots to prepare the qpbt project for palomar". Read this whole file
     5	first. It overrides every older handoff, goal text and briefing, including the error-bounds briefing of
     6	2026-09-29 (that job is finished: PRs #731, #736, #742). The Mac session does no concrete work and is retired
     7	once you are running. All of the work below is yours.
     8	
     9	## 1. The aim
    10	
    11	Thomas Vidick proposed putting the MIP* = RE formalization and its pieces (the LIDT, the compression theorem,
    12	our QPBT) into public collections of formalizations. Palomar (https://palomar-registry.org) is a registry of
    13	Lean-verified mathematics, run with the Lean FRO; it re-checks a submission with the official comparator and
    14	publishes the exact statement. The LIDT is already prepared for it in https://github.com/LionSR/LDT-comparator
    15	(thin wrapper, `formalization.yaml`, single-file `Challenge.lean` of 805 lines).
    16	
    17	**Goal:** make https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator a Palomar-ready thin wrapper for the QPBT
    18	library https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-QPBT, so that the owner only has to open the submission form
    19	and paste one commit SHA. **You do not submit.** Palomar says "Machines should not drive the form", and
    20	submitting is the owner's act.
    21	
    22	## 2. Palomar's requirements (summary made 2026-10-01; the live pages override it)
    23	
    24	Read https://palomar-registry.org/how-to-submit yourself first (curl it), plus any page it links for the
    25	mechanical checks, the agent protocol and the `formalization.yaml` schema. As read on 2026-10-01:
    26	- The submitted repository needs exactly one lakefile, a `lean-toolchain` pinned to a supported Lean release,
    27	  a Challenge module, a Solution module, a comparator JSON config, `formalization.yaml`, and one licence file
    28	  at the root.
    29	- **Challenge:** at most 1,000 lines and 100 KiB (hard); 300 lines and 32 KiB is what they prefer to review. Its
    30	  transitive imports must resolve to Lean core or the pinned, allowlisted Mathlib or Tau Ceti, and nothing else.
    31	  Our current challenge is `Challenge.lean` (225 lines) plus 30 mirror modules under `Challenge/` (3,731
    32	  lines), so it fails both rules and must become one Mathlib-only file within the limit.
    33	- Every regular Lean file **in the submitted repository** must use `module` and have at most 10,000 lines.
    34	  Solution-only dependencies may be arbitrary pinned Git dependencies, so the library itself is probably exempt;
    35	  confirm this on the live page.
    36	- Solution: only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`; no `sorryAx`, no `Lean.ofReduceBool`, no
    37	  custom axioms.
    38	- A thin wrapper names the substantive repository at an immutable commit and the people responsible for it.
    39	- Two checks run on submission: the comparator (mechanical) and an LLM check that the informal descriptions in
    40	  `formalization.yaml` match the formal statements. Write the descriptions so that this check passes honestly.
    41	- The `formalization.yaml` schema: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mathlib-initiative/formalization.yaml/main/schema/formalization.schema.json
    42	  (LDT-comparator's file is a worked example; read it, do not copy its people).
    43	
    44	## 3. What to deliver
    45	
    46	1. **QPBT-comparator `main`**, ready to submit:
    47	   - one Mathlib-only `Challenge.lean`, within the hard limit and as close to 300 lines as faithfulness allows,
    48	     stating the four registered results with `sorry`: `exists_spcc_value_one` (lem:pauli-completeness),
    49	     `exists_ld_soundness` (lem:ld-soundness), `pauli_soundness` (thm:pauli), `pauli_soundness_qubit`
    50	     (cor:pauli-binary);
    51	   - `Solution.lean`, `comparator.json`, `formalization.yaml` (valid against the schema), `LICENSE`,
    52	     `lean-toolchain`, `module` headers wherever Palomar requires them;
    53	   - the library dependency on the current URL https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-QPBT (the pin still uses
    54	     the old name MIPStarRE-A at `ecb97d1f`), pinned to a commit on the library's `main`.
    55	2. **The official comparator run green** in QPBT-comparator's CI (nanoda on, as in run 35638601720), on the
    56	   final commit.
    57	3. **A local check of every mechanical requirement** of section 2 (sizes, imports, `module`, axioms, schema
    58	   validation), with its output kept in the repository.
    59	4. **A submission note for the owner**, `docs/palomar-submission.md` in MIPStarRE-QPBT: the commit SHA to
    60	   submit, the form's URL, what each field should say, what is left for the owner to decide, and any risk
    61	   (for example a requirement you could not check). Plain language, one screen.
    62	
    63	How to shrink the challenge is your design decision. The comparator requires every declaration the statement
    64	uses to be identical in the Challenge and Solution environments. Two known routes:
    65	- (a) trim the definitional closure of the four statements, in the library or by a Mathlib-only statement
    66	  file there, like Vidick's `MIPRE/HaltingGameValue.lean`;
    67	- (b) state slimmer, equivalent definitions in the challenge and prove the bridge inside the Solution, which
    68	  Palomar allows.
    69	
    70	**Faithfulness comes first.** The condensed statements must still say what thm:pauli, cor:pauli-binary,
    71	lem:pauli-completeness and lem:ld-soundness say in arXiv:2001.04383v3, with the same parameters, error form
    72	and quantifier order as today's registered statements. Have an astra worker review the final `Challenge.lean`
    73	against the paper and the current statements before the PR merges.
    74	
    75	## 4. Layout and machinery (set up for you; do not change it)
    76	
    77	- You run on the **space-3 key**, in your own codex home `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/codex-home-qpbt-space3`, with
    78	  full access (the owner's standing permission of 2026-09-19). Multi-agent is off.
    79	- **Three worker slots**, all on the same space-3 key: `keyrot/qpbt-space3` limit 3; caps primary 3 / second 0 /
    80	  total 3. Start workers only through `local/bin/dispatch.sh` and reviews through `local/bin/review.sh`.
    81	- **Models (owner):** you are gpt-6-astra (ultra). **Almost all workers are gpt-5.6-sol** (the default routing):
    82	  Lean writing, debugging, the module and toolchain chores, scripts, `formalization.yaml`, reviews of
    83	  mechanical PRs. Use astra (`--job-class hard --hardness-reason "owner 2026-10-01: statement faithfulness for
    84	  the Palomar challenge"`; for reviews `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_JOB_CLASS=hard_review` and
    85	  `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_HARDNESS_REASON=...`) only where mathematical judgement is needed, such as deciding a
    86	  condensed statement is faithful. Never rewrite models in the shim.
    87	- The space-3 key is shared with the owner's other projects in `~/decoy`, `~/qkd` and `~/jordan-rounding`.
    88	  Never touch those directories, their tmux sessions (`decoy`, `jordan`, `qkd`, `ldt`, `ldt-paper`), their
    89	  codex homes (`codex-home-space-3`, `~/.codex-space-d2`) or their processes, merge daemons and keepers.
    90	- The ghz checkout `~/QPBT-comparator` is on `draft-challenge` with uncommitted files. Leave it as it is and
    91	  work in a fresh clone or worktree.
    92	- **No merge daemon runs for this project.** As in the last job, you may run `local/bin/pr_merge.py` yourself
    93	  on a MIPStarRE-QPBT PR whose gate passes (green CI and an approving review on the exact head). Never use an
    94	  override flag. For QPBT-comparator, merge only when its comparator CI is green and a review approved the
    95	  exact head. That repository's `main` must always equal the latest verified challenge (standing rule of
    96	  2026-09-22).
    97	- The goal keeper is up: it resumes a stalled goal and interrupts a turn longer than 30 minutes. Keep turns
    98	  short. Before your final `/goal pause`, run `touch ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/goal-keeper.stop`, so that
    99	  the keeper does not resume you.
   100	- If the space-3 key fails (a quota or auth error from a direct request, not one flaky reply): post one plain
   101	  comment on issue #27 and `/goal pause`. Never switch keys.
   102	
   103	## 5. Hard rules
   104	
   105	1. **Do not submit to Palomar** or any other registry, and do not use its agent protocol. Do not post on Zulip,
   106	   and do not contact Palomar, Prove2Me, Vidick, Sirui Lu or anyone else.
   107	2. **Never touch github.com/LionSR/** (MIPStarRE, LDT-comparator) or github.com/vidick/: read only, as references.
   108	   Never read or cite `vidick/MIPRE-proof` (private).
   109	3. The four registered results keep their meaning. Any library change goes through the normal gate: zero
   110	   `sorry` on `main`, no new axiom, `lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.AxiomAudit` green.
   111	4. Do not bump the library's Lean or Mathlib version, and do not convert the library to `module`, unless
   112	   Palomar requires it for a Solution-only dependency. If it does, stop: write the cost into the submission
   113	   note, post a ten-line blocker on #500, and `/goal pause`. That is a decision for the owner.
   114	5. `formalization.yaml` people, licence and review status: fill in what the repository shows; the owner's name is
   115	   Ruixuan Deng. Say plainly that the work is AI-generated and has had no human review beyond the owner's
   116	   decisions. List every field the owner must confirm in the submission note.
   117	6. Leave other open work (#734, #735, kit adoption #741, the paused documentary rows) as it is.
   118	
   119	## 6. Stopping rule
   120	
   121	When all four deliverables of section 3 are done, stop: touch `goal-keeper.stop`, post a two-line plain note on
   122	#27 (what is ready, the SHA to submit), and `/goal pause`. Do not start anything else.
   123	
   124	## 7. Talking to the owner
   125	
   126	- At the pause, and if something blocks you, a short plain note on #27; the owner reads GitHub.
   127	- If you need the owner (keys, money, the machine, a decision outside this repository), post a plain blocker of at
   128	  most ten lines on issue #500 and continue with independent work.

./references/qpbt-paper/03_proof_overview.tex:90:We say a few words about the design of $\mu'$ and the associated introspection game, which borrow heavily from~\cite{NW19}. Building on the ``quantum low-degree test'' introduced in~\cite{natarajan2018low} it is already known how a verifier can force a pair of players to measure $m$ EPR pairs in either the computational or Hadamard basis and report the (necessarily identical) outcome $z$ obtained, all the while using questions of length polylogarithmic in $m$ only. The added difficulty is to ensure that a player obtains, and returns, precisely the information about $z$ that is contained in $L^\alice(z)$ (resp. $L^\bob(z)$), and not more. A simple example is the line-point distribution described earlier: there, the idea to ensure that e.g.\ the ``point'' player only obtains the first component, $x$ of $(x,v) \in V_\xpt \oplus V_{\dir{}}$, the verifier demands that the ``point'' player measures their qubits associated with the space $V_{\dir{}}$ in the Hadamard, instead of computational, basis; due to the uncertainty principle this has the effect of ``erasing'' the outcome in the computational basis.  The case of the ``line'' player is a little more complex: the goal is to ensure that, conditioned on the specification of the line $\ell$ received by the ``line'' player, the point $x$ received by the ``point'' player is uniformly random within $\ell$. This was shown to be possible in~\cite{NW19}.

     9	#                       [--force-review] [--dry-run]
    10	#
    11	#   <pr-number>      GitHub PR number ("12").  Branch, base and head SHA come
    12	#                    from gh_common.py pr-view; the local branch tip must be
    13	#                    exactly the GitHub head before anything is reviewed.
    14	#   --force-review   Review even when the head commit is a bot fix commit.
    15	#                    Used by autofix.sh for the single forced review at the
    16	#                    iteration cap (local/protocols/autofix.md).
    17	#   --dry-run        Resolve the worktree, diff and prompts, print where they
    18	#                    landed, and stop before dispatching an agent.
    19	#   --source-repo    Review Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator from this clean checkout.
    20	#                    The checkout, PR repository, branch, base and exact head
    21	#                    must agree; official comparator CI replaces local CI.
    22	#
    23	# Local replacement for .github/workflows/pr-review.yml (gate + code-review +
    24	# prose-review jobs).  Protocol: local/protocols/review.md.
    25	#
    26	# GitHub is the record (gh_common.py:4-8).  The gate reads exact-head CI:
    27	# local-ci/summary for the library, or the official NanoDa-enabled comparator
    28	# check for the explicit companion route.  The verdict is published as ONE
    29	# COMMENT review bound to that SHA plus a local-review/summary status.
    30	# Single-account repos cannot self-APPROVE, so adverseness travels in the
    31	# status, never in a review state.  There is no local PR record: a GitHub
    32	# failure fails this script closed rather than leaving a fallback record.
    33	#
    34	# Exit codes:
    35	#   0  review published, or an intentional skip (kill switch, bot commit, stale
    36	#      head, empty diff)
    37	#   1  usage or environment error
    38	#   3  gate blocked: required exact-head CI is absent or not successful.
    39	#      Nothing is published — absence of local-review/summary is the block.
    40	#   4  the reviewer returned no machine-parseable verdict trailer.  A failing
    41	#      local-review/summary is posted so the PR never reads as green.
    42	#
    43	# Environment:
    44	#   LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED       disables the reviewer on the literal string
    45	#                              "false" only; unset means enabled.
    46	#   MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF      git ref the reviewer personas are read from
    47	#                              (default: main).  Never the branch under review.
    48	#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL     codex model for the code review
    49	#                              (auto: routine Sol, justified hard Astra)
    50	#   MIPSTARRE_PROSE_MODEL      codex model for the blueprint prose review
    51	#                              (default: MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL)
    52	#   MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT        runtime state root (default ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev)
    53	#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_LOCK_WAIT seconds to queue behind another review of the
    54	#                              same PR before giving up (default 1800)
    55	#   MIPSTARRE_DIFF_MAX_LINES   diff lines handed to the reviewer (default 4000)
    56	#   MIPSTARRE_CITATION_MAX_BYTES bytes reserved for the derived blueprint
    57	#                              citation map (default 30000)
    58	#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_TIMEOUT   reviewer safety timeout in seconds (default 10800)
    59	#   MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_EFFORT    ultra (required, default)
    60	#   MIPSTARRE_NATIVE_REVIEW_ROOT
    61	#   MIPSTARRE_NATIVE_REVIEW_AUTHORS
    62	#                              retired legacy routing variables; ignored for
    63	#                              current reviews. Unset both before operation.
    64	#   MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO      owner/repo override for gh_common.py
    65	#                              (must be Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator when
    66	#                              --source-repo is used)
    67	#
    68	set -euo pipefail

   181	# sanitize_to <src> <dest> <max-lines> [max-bytes] — control-char strip, fence
   182	# breaking, and bounded output (DESIGN.md invariant 6).  A zero bound disables
   183	# that dimension. dispatch.sh sanitizes attachments again; this copy also
   184	# protects the no-dispatcher fallback path.
   185	sanitize_to() {
   186	  python3 - "$1" "$2" "$3" "${4:-0}" <<'PY'
   187	import sys
   188	src, dest = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   189	max_lines, max_bytes = int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4])
   190	try:
   191	    raw = open(src, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
   192	except OSError:
   193	    raw = ""
   194	raw = raw.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
   195	keep = []
   196	for ch in raw:
   197	    o = ord(ch)
   198	    if ch in "\n\t" or (32 <= o < 127) or o > 159:
   199	        keep.append(ch)
   200	lines = "".join(keep).split("\n")
   201	truncated = 0
   202	if max_lines > 0 and len(lines) > max_lines:
   203	    truncated = len(lines) - max_lines
   204	    lines = lines[:max_lines]
   205	out = []
   206	for line in lines:
   207	    line = line.replace("```", "'''").replace("~~~", "'''")
   208	    if line.startswith("<<<") or line.startswith("# Task"):
   209	        line = " " + line
   210	    out.append(line)
   211	if truncated:
   212	    out.append("... [%d further lines omitted by review.sh; full text on disk]"
   213	               % truncated)
   214	rendered = "\n".join(out) + "\n"
   215	encoded = rendered.encode("utf-8")
   216	if max_bytes > 0 and len(encoded) > max_bytes:
   217	    marker = b"\n... [truncated by review.sh attachment budget; full text on disk]\n"
   218	    keep_bytes = max(0, max_bytes - len(marker))
   219	    prefix = encoded[:keep_bytes].decode("utf-8", errors="ignore").rstrip()
   220	    rendered = prefix + marker.decode("ascii")
   220	    rendered = prefix + marker.decode("ascii")
   221	open(dest, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(rendered)
   222	PY
   223	}

   225	# acquire_lock <lockdir> <wait-seconds> <label>
   226	# Per-PR review lock.  No cancellation: a queued review waits and then
   227	# re-checks the head SHA (pr-review.yml:18-20, cancel-in-progress false).
   228	acquire_lock() {
   229	  local dir="$1" wait_s="$2" label="$3" waited=0 holder=""
   230	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dir")"
   231	  while ! mkdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null; do
   232	    holder="$(cat "$dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   233	    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
   234	      warn "removing stale lock $dir (holder pid $holder is gone)"
   235	      rm -rf "$dir"
   236	      continue
   237	    fi
   238	    if [ "$waited" -ge "$wait_s" ]; then
   239	      die "timed out after ${wait_s}s waiting for the review lock $dir (holder pid ${holder:-unknown})"
   240	    fi
   241	    [ "$waited" = 0 ] && log "another review holds $dir (pid ${holder:-unknown}); queuing"
   242	    sleep 5
   243	    waited=$((waited + 5))
   244	  done
   245	  printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$dir/pid"
   246	  printf '%s\n' "$label" >"$dir/label"
   247	  LOCK_HELD="$dir"
   248	}

   261	# git_remote_slug <checkout> — canonical owner/repo from the explicit origin.
   262	# The companion route must not let MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO point API reads at one
   263	# repository while the reviewer inspects bytes from another.
   264	git_remote_slug() {
   265	  local url
   266	  url="$(git -C "$1" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || true)"
   267	  [ -n "$url" ] || return 1
   268	  python3 - "$url" <<'PY'
   269	import re, sys
   270	patterns = (
   271	    r"^(?:[^@]+@)?github\.com:([^/]+/[^/\s]+?)(?:\.git)?/?$",
   272	    r"^(?:https?|ssh|git)://(?:[^@/]+@)?github\.com/"
   273	    r"([^/]+/[^/\s]+?)(?:\.git)?/?$",
   274	)
   275	for pattern in patterns:
   276	    match = re.match(pattern, sys.argv[1])
   277	    if match:
   278	        print(match.group(1))
   279	        break
   280	else:
   281	    raise SystemExit(1)
   282	PY
   283	}

   285	# validate_source_checkout — fail closed before consuming external CI evidence.
   286	validate_source_checkout() {
   287	  local top slug current_branch current_head branch_tip base_tip dirty
   288	  top="$(git -C "$REVIEW_ROOT" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
   289	  [ -n "$top" ] || die "--source-repo $REVIEW_ROOT is not a Git checkout"
   290	  top="$(cd "$top" && pwd -P)"
   291	  [ "$top" = "$REVIEW_ROOT" ] ||
   292	    die "--source-repo must name the checkout root exactly (got $REVIEW_ROOT, root is $top)"
   293	  slug="$(git_remote_slug "$REVIEW_ROOT" || true)"
   294	  [ "$slug" = "$TARGET_REPO" ] ||
   295	    die "source checkout origin is '${slug:-unrecognized}', not target repository $TARGET_REPO"
   296	  [ "$PR_HEAD_REPO" = "$TARGET_REPO" ] ||
   297	    die "PR #$PR_NUM head repository is '${PR_HEAD_REPO:-missing}', expected $TARGET_REPO"
   298	  [ "$PR_BASE_REPO" = "$TARGET_REPO" ] ||
   299	    die "PR #$PR_NUM base repository is '${PR_BASE_REPO:-missing}', expected $TARGET_REPO"
   300	
   301	  current_branch="$(git -C "$REVIEW_ROOT" symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
   302	  [ "$current_branch" = "$BRANCH" ] ||
   303	    die "source checkout is on '${current_branch:-detached HEAD}'," \
   304	      "but PR #$PR_NUM head branch is '$BRANCH'"
   305	  current_head="$(git -C "$REVIEW_ROOT" rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD^{commit} || true)"
   306	  [ "$current_head" = "$HEAD_SHA" ] ||
   307	    die "source checkout HEAD is ${current_head:-unreadable}, but PR #$PR_NUM head is $HEAD_SHA"
   308	  branch_tip="$(git -C "$REVIEW_ROOT" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$BRANCH^{commit}" || true)"
   309	  [ "$branch_tip" = "$HEAD_SHA" ] ||
   310	    die "source branch '$BRANCH' is ${branch_tip:-missing}, but PR #$PR_NUM head is $HEAD_SHA"
   311	  base_tip="$(git -C "$REVIEW_ROOT" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$BASE^{commit}" || true)"
   312	  [ -n "$base_tip" ] || die "source base branch '$BASE' does not resolve"
   313	  [ "$base_tip" = "$BASE_SHA" ] ||
   314	    die "source base '$BASE' is $base_tip, but PR #$PR_NUM base is $BASE_SHA;" \
   315	      "fetch the exact PR base"
   316	  dirty="$(git -C "$REVIEW_ROOT" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)"
   317	  [ -z "$dirty" ] || die "source checkout $REVIEW_ROOT is dirty;" \
   318	    "companion reviews require a clean exact-head tree:
   319	$dirty"
   320	}

   331	# resolve_worktree <branch> — same resolution order as ci.sh: git's own
   332	# registry first, then the .worktrees/<branch> convention.  Creates it if the
   333	# branch has no worktree yet.
   334	resolve_worktree() {
   335	  local branch="$1" found="" safe dest have
   336	  found="$(git -C "$ROOT" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null |
   337	    awk -v b="refs/heads/$branch" '
   338	      /^worktree /{p=substr($0,10)}
   339	      $0 == "branch " b {print p; exit}')"
   340	  if [ -n "$found" ] && [ -d "$found" ]; then
   341	    printf '%s\n' "$found"
   342	    return 0
   343	  fi
   344	  safe="$(printf '%s' "$branch" | tr '/' '-')"
   345	  dest="$ROOT/.worktrees/$safe"
   346	  if [ -e "$dest" ]; then
   347	    have="$(git -C "$dest" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
   348	    if [ "$have" = "$branch" ]; then
   349	      printf '%s\n' "$dest"
   350	      return 0
   351	    fi
   352	    die "$dest exists but is not a worktree of '$branch' (HEAD: ${have:-not a git worktree}); run 'git -C $ROOT worktree prune' or remove it"
   353	  fi
   354	  mkdir -p "$ROOT/.worktrees"
   355	  git -C "$ROOT" worktree add --quiet "$dest" "$branch" ||
   356	    die "git worktree add $dest $branch failed"
   357	  if [ -x "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" ]; then
   358	    "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" "$dest" >&2 ||
   359	      warn "worktree-setup.sh failed for $dest; the reviewer runs without a warmed build cache"
   360	  else
   361	    warn "local/bin/worktree-setup.sh not found; the reviewer worktree has no warmed Lean build cache (local/protocols/build-cache.md)"
   362	  fi
   363	  printf '%s\n' "$dest"
   364	}

   366	# run_agent <role> <sandbox> <worktree> <persona-path> <task-file>
   367	#           <context-file> <out-file> <model>
   368	#
   369	# All codex invocations go through local/bin/dispatch.sh, so the session lands
   370	# in results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl (DESIGN.md, "Agent sessions").
   371	run_agent() {
   372	  local role="$1" sandbox="$2" wt="$3" persona="$4" taskfile="$5"
   373	  local ctx="$6" out="$7" model="$8"
   374	  local dlog="$out.dispatch.log" task_text last rc=0
   375	  model="$(python3 "$BIN_DIR/model_policy.py" "${REVIEW_POLICY_ARGS[@]}" \
   376	    --model "$model" --effort "$REVIEW_EFFORT" --field model)" || return 4
   377	  task_text="$(cat "$taskfile")"
   378	
   379	  if [ -x "$DISPATCH" ]; then
   380	    local args
   381	    args=(--role "$role" --issue "$REVIEW_SCOPE" --pr "$PR_NUM"
   382	          --worktree "$wt" --sandbox "$sandbox"
   383	          --persona "$persona" --persona-ref "$TRUSTED_REF"
   384	          --effort "$REVIEW_EFFORT")
   385	    args+=(--job-class "$REVIEW_JOB_CLASS")
   386	    [ -z "$REVIEW_HARDNESS_REASON" ] || args+=(--hardness-reason "$REVIEW_HARDNESS_REASON")
   387	    # The bounded citation map goes first so dispatch.sh's aggregate attachment
   388	    # cap cannot let a large diff starve it from the reviewer context.
   389	    if [ -s "$BLUEPRINT_CITATION_MAP" ]; then
   390	      args[${#args[@]}]="--context-file"
   391	      args[${#args[@]}]="$BLUEPRINT_CITATION_MAP"
   392	    fi
   393	    if [ -n "$ctx" ]; then
   394	      args[${#args[@]}]="--context-file"
   395	      args[${#args[@]}]="$ctx"
   396	    fi
   397	    if [ -s "$RUN_DIR/prior-ledger.md" ]; then
   398	      args[${#args[@]}]="--context-file"
   399	      args[${#args[@]}]="$RUN_DIR/prior-ledger.md"
   400	    fi
   401	    args[${#args[@]}]="--"
   402	    args[${#args[@]}]="$task_text"
   403	    # One retry for pre-model failures: a dispatch that dies within seconds
   404	    # with zero tokens never reached the model (transient CLI/API hiccup;
   405	    # observed on PR #0003, events.md 2026-08-31), so retrying cannot
   406	    # duplicate a review.
   407	    local attempt started ended tokens
   408	    for attempt in 1 2; do
   409	      started="$(date +%s)"
   410	      set +e
   411	      if [ -n "$model" ]; then
   412	        MIPSTARRE_SESSION_TIMEOUT="$REVIEW_TIMEOUT" MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 \
   413	          MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL="$model" "$DISPATCH" "${args[@]}" >"$dlog"
   414	      else
   415	        MIPSTARRE_SESSION_TIMEOUT="$REVIEW_TIMEOUT" MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 \
   416	          "$DISPATCH" "${args[@]}" >"$dlog"
   417	      fi
   418	      rc=$?
   419	      set -e
   420	      ended="$(date +%s)"
   421	      tokens="$(sed -n 's/^tokens_total: //p' "$dlog" | tail -1)"
   422	      if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && [ "$attempt" -eq 1 ] \

   432	### Owner-authorized mixed-model review (2026-09-17; issue #575)
   433	
   434	The owner authorized six helper slots on the owner's Mac: **three fixers and

   482	The remainder of this subsection records the former transport for interpreting

   491	green exact-head CI. `native_review.py request` creates a nonce-bound request under

    12	# from this trusted checkout.

The report artifact, not hand-supplied status fields, is authoritative and binds repository, commit, selected paths, workflow run/revision, hashes, declarations, dependencies, and exact tools. I’m checking for a locally cached verifier checkout to pin the precise JSON keys before finalizing that finding.
